- 2026-10-02 10:05 key 20261002T0754-rknh by unrecorded · 075 review changes · by rev-runes-016 (fresh) · Important: part a regresses an edge 1.0.0 reports. When a web node declares the global Program explicitly ('public partial class Program { }', the documented WebApplicationFactory pattern for .NET 6-9) and ANY other node has top-level statements (Aspire AppHost, a worker, a migrator), the implicit key from that other file makes 'Program' two-owner ambiguous and the test -> web edge goes silent. Repro <the session scratchpad, since lost>/patch-611/review-016-csharp-refs/after/probe/partial.mjs (web top-level + partial, apphost top-level, tests WebApplicationFactory<Program>): base edge tests -> web at ApiTests.cs:4, branch []. Real repo: bug-hunt verify-44 ca-partial-web (CleanArchitecture with the partial in Web) under yg 6.1.0: base reports Application-FunctionalTests -> Web at WebApiFactory.cs:10, the branch's csharp.mjs drops it. The same holds for a classic global 'class Program { static Main }' next to any top-level file elsewhere. This is a behaviour trade-off patch-scope sends to the owner, and the changelog fragment hides it ('stays silent' reads as no change). Either avoid it (let the implicit Program yield to an explicit global Program, e.g. publish it under an internal fallback key that the bare 'Program' reference tries only after the verbatim key is absent; no new export needed), or ask the owner and state the lost edge in the fragment.

- 2026-10-02 10:17 key 20261002T0722-lboi by unrecorded · 011 review changes · by rev-runes-010 (fresh) · Important: holds() passes the default include (no files, no include) through asDirectory(configDir), and asDirectory treats a last segment with a dot as a file pattern, so a config in a directory like apps/web.v2 holds nothing by default; tsc's default is **/* under the config and ignores the name. Effects, each checked against tsc 6.0.3 --listFilesOnly: (a) regression on a non-solution layout, a false edge: apps/web.v2/tsconfig.json with its own paths @/* -> ./src/*, no include, references ./tsconfig.node.json (include **/*.ts, paths -> ./build/*): 1.0.0 and tsc give apps/web.v2/src/m.ts, the branch gives apps/web.v2/build/m.ts; (b) a solution root in a dotted dir whose default-include config and a second config both hold the file with different paths: tsc has two disagreeing holders (ruling: silence), the branch binds the second; (c) a lone default-include referenced config in a dotted dir is never a holder (silence). Fix, verified to cure all three: const include = config.include ?? (config.files === undefined ? [configDir === '' ? '**/*' : `${configDir}/**/*`] : []); plus a unit test. Repro: scratchpad patch-611/review-010-ts-resolve/probe011/probe2.mjs (S14) and probe.mjs (S1, S5).

- 2026-10-02 10:48 key 20261002T0958-hsbn by unrecorded · 149 review changes · by rev-runes-135 (fresh) · Important: CRLF regression in tomlLogicalLines + KEY_VALUE. A joined logical line keeps each line's \r (only the \n becomes a space), and KEY_VALUE's (.*)$ cannot cross a \r, so any CRLF entry whose inline table holds a multi-line array no longer matches at all. Before 5be4794 the first physical line was read; now the whole entry is dropped: kit = { workspace = true, features = [\r\n "x",\r\n] } (zed's crates/zed gpui_platform shape) or a path written before the array loses the crate, and the 149 shape itself (path after the array) is still silent on CRLF. Evidence: disk-backed CRLF workspace (<the session scratchpad, since lost>/patch-611/review-135-cargo-manifest/crlf-ws, crlf-edge.mjs): kit::Engine from crates/app/src/main.rs binds crates/kit/src/lib.rs on fbc0539 and is undefined on 462c70c. The worker's 344-file corpus converted to CRLF (diff-cargo-eol.mjs, corpus-crlf.log): base 2 disagreements with smol-toml, head 31 new (17 workspace deps in zed/Cargo.toml incl. reqwest, gpui_platform workspace=true in crates/zed, xim and 6 more in gpui_linux, ...); LF stays new=0 fixed=2. A Windows checkout with autocrlf gives exactly this. Fix: treat \r\n as the newline in tomlLogicalLines (or let the value capture [\s\S]*), plus a CRLF unit case (path before and after a multi-line array).

Probes, base -> head: [lib] path=lib.rs + [[bin]] path=main.rs, crate::Config from library module foo.rs: lib.rs -> main.rs (decoy, main.rs shadows Config); crate::LibOnly: lib.rs -> undefined. [lib] path=lib/lib.rs + [[bin]] path=main.rs: crate::Item from lib/util.rs: lib/lib.rs -> main.rs (decoy); crate::util from lib/other.rs: lib/lib.rs -> util.rs (the binary's module, decoy). [lib] and [[bin]] both in crates/core: crate::Item from crates/core/util.rs: crates/core/lib.rs -> undefined. Fix: let the library root's directory compete in the deepest-directory choice (a file under the lib's directory keeps the library tree; same directory as a bin -> both roots, like src/'s [lib, main], or fail closed).

- 2026-10-02 12:11 key 20261002T0737-hcph by unrecorded · 048 review changes · by rev-grain-048 (fresh) · Important: cb3e416 moves file co-change for completeness, check, review, the hooks and where from the whole history to the newest 20 000 non-bulk commits. Before, model.cochange/nonMegaCommits/fileTouches came from the walk's running counts (history.mjs replay: state.pairSup/fileCommits/fileOthers, never truncated); now applyFileCochange counts H.fps, which history.mjs truncates to CFG.fpsCap = 20000. This is a new limit for these surfaces (grain cochange always had it). On any repository with more than 20 000 non-bulk commits, partners whose co-change is older than the window vanish and every count and base rate shifts. Shown on scratch copies of both trees with fpsCap lowered to 30 (x.js+y.js together 10 times, then 40 other commits): release/6.1.1 names y.js 11/11, the branch names nothing (scratch: <the session scratchpad, since lost>/patch-611/review-048-cochange-one-population, make-old.sh, cap30-*). Not asked by the acceptance, not raised to the owner (patch-scope: a behaviour change with a real trade-off goes to him as a question), absent from the changelog entry, and docs/mathematics.md:292 still says fpsCap is a compute guard on which no claim rests. An alternative exists: footprints list only the new path of a rename (fps {files:[mid/a.js], renames:[[src/a.js, mid/a.js]]}), so the walk's un-floored full-history counts could be carried through currentPathOf before the floor, with its own edge cases (a commit naming two historical paths that resolve to one). Either ask the owner and disclose the window in the changelog and mathematics.md, or keep the full-history population.

So when an edit turns a declaration's only (or topmost) decorator into a comment or a blank line, or deletes it while a comment sits between it and the declaration, the declaration is no longer in the change and the deviation the edit made is filed as pre-existing. Fixture cart.handler.ts line 6 '@Handler()' -> '// @Handler()': before '1 deviation(s) in your change', and the check-hook says 'Your type CreateCartHandler (line 7) is not annotated with @Handler'; after '0 deviation(s) in your change, 1 pre-existing' and the hook is silent. The same happens when line 6 is blanked, and when '@Handler()' is deleted with '// eslint-disable-next-line ...' committed between it and the class. Real repo, flask d73fa1c tests/conftest.py:37 '@pytest.fixture' -> '# @pytest.fixture': before '1 deviation(s) in your change ... Your method app_ctx (line 38) is not annotated with @pytest.fixture' and the hook speaks; after '0 deviation(s) in your change, 2 pre-existing' and the hook gives only the co-change line. Acceptance 3 ('a change to or a deletion of the @Handler() itself is still attributed to the class') fails for the commonest way to switch a decorator off. By construction the same holds for Java/C#/Kotlin/PHP annotations: once commented out, the comment sits outside the declaration's node. The tests cover only a decorator swapped for another (D) and a deletion directly above the class (D2). Possible fix: also count a hunk whose removed lines lay on the scope's stack at HEAD (the pre-image), or let the head extend over the comment lines directly attached to it.

Reproduced: lock '99999\nsome-container' -> grain status still waiting after 6 s. With a 30 s heartbeat the foreign-host staleness window can be a few heartbeats; release on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP; name .grain/cache/build.lock in the waiting line. Hooks are not affected (they never take the lock; check-hook exit 0 while the lock was held).

A TypeScript declaration file without import/export (global.d.ts, env.d.ts: 'declare global {...}', 'interface Foo {}') gets g=typescript, esm=false, directive='none'. The result is a false-red after adoption on a file where the directive means nothing, and the changelog line 'no longer counts TypeScript ... files' is false for it. The fill runs the script but writeOrRemoveSplitFile refuses to write .yg-lock.deterministic.json, so even this run's own verdicts are thrown away. A fresh container checkout with dubious ownership plus script rules is therefore always red. Suggest: when git can't be asked, distrust only what was on disk before the run (or skip just the read) while still writing and using this run's own verdicts. Or decide to accept the red and put it in the Before-you-upgrade note.

Probe on the tip: a conflicted merge finished with git commit, then 'yg check --approve' run straight away exits 0, PASS, and closes the cycle. The following 'yg check' is PASS, the merged log keeps a branch's entry as its newest, and the owed entry was never asked for. That is the very 'easy to skip' of the Why. --approve has to refuse (or stop at) the same unreconciled merge the plain check flags.

- 2026-10-04 22:55 key 20261002T1101-mmvb by unrecorded · 166 review changes · by rev-ygg-166 (fresh) · Important: nested re-include of a DIRECTORY is not honoured for files below it. Repro (from fuzz vs git check-ignore --no-index, git 2.55, tracked and untracked, ignorecase true and false): root .gitignore 'a/', Sub/.gitignore '!a/', file Sub/a/n.txt -> git keeps it, isFileGitignored=true and walkRepoFiles drops it. Same with root 'build/' + b/gen/.gitignore '!*/'. Cause: stackIgnores asks each layer about the leaf, and node-ignore's test() checks the leaf's parent dirs inside that shallow layer ('a/' matches), so the shallow layer's inherited verdict wins after the deeper layer already re-included the directory; the ancestor loop got the directory right. Fix direction: once the ancestor loop clears every ancestor, a layer's verdict that comes only from a parent directory must not count (e.g. skip a layer whose test(parentDir/) is ignored). Add that case to the parity test.

- 2026-10-05 14:58 key 20261004T2055-pjbm by unrecorded · 221 review changes · by rev-ygg-221 (fresh) · Important — (b) is a false red: after a rebase, the entry the message asks for, committed without a fill (the documented log-cycle-open state), is still log-entry-missing in every clone, and yg check --approve refuses over it (reproduced: log add, commit, check FAIL, approve exit 1). To clear it the user has to write a second entry and fill before committing. The message says the newest entry 'was committed with that history rather than written for it', which is false here, and the CHANGELOG line 'an entry of its own settles it' is false once committed. The node log says a replayed entry and a later one cannot be told apart, but they can: a replayed entry predates the combining commit's committer date, and a later entry postdates it.

The cli-lock-scope budget of 180 s only stops a hung case: every assertion is unchanged, and the global testTimeout of 30000 still covers the rest; the other heavy e2e suites use 240 s. reference-truth and lock-scope pass 9/9 on the tip.

- 2026-10-08 11:45 by unrecorded · asked a-018 (charter) · 6.2.0 growth, all of it in one question (the design research/2026-10-08-jarl-field-report-and-repository-names/design.md, Proposed changes, built on a field report from a loop in another project): beyond the Jarl scope you approved in a-002, the design proposes (1) in 246, that a merge no longer records its CI as pending by default but only when a run will report, that a merge which lands while its check is red for a cause outside the branch is recorded with --red naming the issue that tracks the cause, and that whether a repository lands on its check is derived from its merge rows instead of a declared Check line; (2) in 244, that one answer can settle several ratify items with one verdict, and that superseding a ruling names the open issues that still cite it; (3) in 250, that the sentence "a compaction is a session start" also goes into the instructions Jarl's MCP server gives the host; (4) issue 280, that show prints by default only what the done gate counts (every row and verdict since the last start, every unanswered finding) and show --full the whole file. Options: (a) all four into 6.2.0: the Jarl part of the release grows, and 247 stays the first item to set aside; (b) none, they go to 6.3.0: until then a merge's CI stays pending or none, both false for a merge that is not pushed, an outside red is charged to the worker as a round, and show grows with 248's full reviews; (c) choose item by item. Recommendation (the architect's design): (a); it proposes every item for 6.2.0 and names the bounded show explicitly, because 248, already in 6.2.0, makes show grow faster.

- 2026-10-11 20:26 by unrecorded · decided hooks-silent-while-refreshing · by jarl
- 2026-10-11 20:26 key 20261005T1413-vrdd by unrecorded · 228 evidence · Ruling hooks-silent-while-refreshing: While a hook-started refresh runs, the edit-time hooks answer nothing; they emit no status marker. The acceptance allows the rest to wait or answer with a marker, and the release plan's defaults allow a marker or silence while refreshing, never the old index. A marker on every edit would put a line into the agent's context on each tool call for the seconds or minutes a refresh takes, and SessionStart already says that the hooks are silent while the index is behind. Waiting would stall the edit. Silence is therefore the answer, and the documentation says so.

- 2026-10-29 14:33 by unrecorded · asked a-026 (charter) · Issues 346 to 354 make every family repository leave only code on the host, and their pattern puts loop workers in clones on a container volume instead of worktrees. The ruling worktrees-follow-gard puts worktrees in .worktrees of the shell on the host, mounted at the same path in the container, which removes the reason for clones (a worktree made inside a container left dangling entries in the host's git) and keeps the rule, because a worktree is code. Options: (a) 346 to 354 adopt Gard's layout and wait for Gard's run and worktree issues (379, 387), so the family moves once; (b) 346 to 354 go ahead now with clones on a volume, and 424 later moves the family to Gard's layout; (c) 346 to 354 do the dev containers now without the worker part, and the worker part waits for Gard. The jarl recommends (c): containers that leave the host clean are needed now for the release's checks, and the workers' place is decided once, by Gard.

- 2026-11-02 21:49 key 20261011T2055-rsvv by unrecorded · 295 review changes · by rev-runes-295-opus (fresh) · Important: the diff makes item 1 of the folded evidence worse in one shape, so item 1 belongs to this issue: namespace A { using O = X.Order; class C { O x; } } namespace B { using O = Y.Order; class D { O y; } } with a global type O now gives the use in A an edge to the global O (false edge); on release/1.1.0 that use was silent. Cause: aliases and aliasScopes are keyed by name and the last directive wins (src/relations/extractors/csharp.mts:505-506), viewAlias then finds B's body outside A and returns undefined, so the verbatim reading binds. Fix: keep one alias entry per directive body and pick the one whose body encloses the use; add a catalogue case for both shapes (with and without a global O) · Minor: item 7 is half done: 13.4 became 14.5 but 13.3 (namespace declarations) and 13.8 (qualified alias member) remain catalogue-wide, and the new case csharp-alias-colon-colon-in-namespace-edge cites 13.8 · Minor: items 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 are untouched behaviour that predates this change; they can split into a new 6.2.0 issue · Acceptance tests 1-3 met, red on the base extractor (3 fail) and green on the branch (140 pass), reproduced · model claude-opus-5-5

- 2026-11-11 10:45 by planner-runes · asked a-33 (charter) · Runes 1.1.0, issue 493 (C#). Inside a class, a name such as User in User.FindFirst("sub") can be a member the class inherits rather than a type; C# then reads the member and the code does not depend on a domain type called User. Where the base class is in the repository, Runes can tell exactly, and the acceptance of 493 now covers that. Where the chain of base classes leaves the repository (ASP.NET Core's ControllerBase, EF Core's DbContext, any package), Runes cannot see the base's members and cannot tell. Today it reads the name as a type, which gives a false edge from every ASP.NET controller that writes User.… to the node that declares a domain User (the audit's probe p42). The same choice decides the twin cases of 494 (a nested type of an outside base) and 498 (an instance method of an outside base, which hides an extension method of that name). Which behaviour should 1.1.0 ship? (a) No edge for any name that could be a member of an outside base: no false edge, but every static call and enum value inside such a class is lost too; a cruder form of this rule lost 2176 references in jellyfin, 50 in CleanArchitecture and 41 in eShop, mostly true ones. (b) Keep reading such a name as a type, as today, and document the false edge as a known limit: no true edge lost, the controller false edge stays, though at node level it is often hidden because a controller usually depends on the domain node anyway. (c) A short, hand-kept list of the public members of the most common outside bases (ASP.NET Core ControllerBase, Controller, PageModel, ComponentBase; EF Core DbContext): those names are read as members in classes derived from them, as C# reads them, and everything else as in (b); it removes the common false edge without losing true ones, at the cost of a list that must follow those frameworks and covers no others. Recommended: (c).

Minor: the grammar misreads more import types than the one form reported, and each is marked as an import call with the same wrong target under nodenext: a class heritage type argument (class declaration, class expression, export default class), a call or tagged-template type argument (g<import("x").T>()), keyof import("x").T, a parenthesized (import("x").T) and a template literal type. As a limit of the grammar it is acceptable, since no type node exists to read, but it is acceptable only written down: docs/api.md:86 and the changelog say an import type reads its file's format without any limit, and the list must name all of these forms. Minor: test/relations/extractors/typescript-conditions-compiler.test.mjs:15,33,97 - the comparison does ask the compiler (createProgram and getResolvedModuleFromModuleSpecifier, no copy of Runes' rule) and fails when either rule is switched off, but it leaves out umd, system, none, the ES kinds, node18, node20, .tsx, .jsx and a package type of commonjs, and its floor of 20 compared rows would hold if most rows fell away; all of those match the compiler when added. Checked and right: finding 1 is closed (typescript-resolve.mts:261 matches the compiler on 180 rows in each of 19 consistent settings); the type side of as, satisfies, a type alias, annotations, type arguments in a parsed position, constraints, defaults, implements, mapped, conditional, indexed, tuple and function types is unmarked, and a value import() beside a type keeps its mark (86 placements compared with the compiler's parser); the extractor rev stays 4 on an unreleased branch; the three commits name both issues and are not amends. - 2026-11-11 11:19 key 20261111T1104-dkel by w-554-fable · 554 evidence · Cause: the test, not Grain. The file's last test puts a stand-in git first on PATH, and the stand-in starts the git that 'which git' names. On a machine whose first git is a wrapper that looks the real git up on PATH (a proxy that checks commits, a version manager's shim), the wrapper finds the stand-in as the real git and the stand-in starts the wrapper again, without end. Each round is a node process of about 19 MB that waits for the next: 107 rounds at the 2 GB kill (9 s), 222 at the 4 GB kill (12 s), no process above 90 MB, which is why no single process looked large. The 21 tests before it pass; the reporter prints nothing later because the kill takes the buffered output. Each Grain command the earlier tests run peaks near 65 MB. Grain's own code cannot loop this way: it starts git by name (26 call sites) and never puts a git of its own on PATH or changes PATH, so under such a wrapper every call goes wrapper, then real git. Fix: a stand-in runs the real git under the PATH without its own directory.
- 2026-11-11 11:19 key 20261111T1104-dkel by w-554-fable · 554 evidence · Assumed: the same fault is fixed in the two other test files that hand calls from a stand-in git to the real git, because the full suite cannot pass on such a machine otherwise: build-coordination (its test (a) did not end within 90 s; a 3 s probe of the pair passed through the stand-in 2405 times, in one process, so no memory grows there) and orphan-child (two tests failed after 30 s and 122 s). The five shell stand-ins now take the real git from one helper, tests/real-git.mjs. After: the four files run 64 tests under a 2 GB cap, peak 312 MB; test (a) ends in 2.3 s.
- 2026-11-11 11:19 key 20261111T1104-dkel by w-554-fable · 554 evidence · Assumed: the fault shows only on a machine with such a wrapper, so two checks build a wrapper of their own that counts its passes and stops with exit 97 on the fourth: one test in review-range-not-an-option for its node stand-in, and a new file, stand-in-git-behind-a-wrapper.test.mjs, for the shell helper. Both were committed failing (exit 97) before their fix and pass after it, on any machine.

Declaration means a top-level mod x; or mod x { } in the root file, read from its text with comments and strings blanked, never one inside another module's braces.

- 2026-11-11 11:29 key 20261103T0440-fikt by rev-509-fable · 509 review changes · by rev-509-fable (fresh) · model claude-fable-5-2 · batch 20261111T1129-zikf · Important (509, src/relations/resolve-path.mts:440 topLevelModules, used at :296 and :322): in a package with src/lib.rs and src/main.rs a module loses every crate:: root-item edge to the library when the root declares it in a way the text reader does not see, where the base bound the library correctly. Reproduced on the built tool against the base: mod unix; inside a cfg_if! block; mod late; after a function holding the char literal '{' ; mod late; after a raw string holding a quote and a brace; #[path = "imp/thing.rs"] mod thing; and a mod written by a macro_rules! expansion. Each gave src/lib.rs before and nothing after. The brace counter treats a char literal and a raw string as code, and a module at brace depth above zero as undeclared. No test covers these; a case for each is needed, and the choice of what a root that cannot be read means (keep the old binding, or silence) belongs in the fix. Important (511, src/relations/extractors/rust-resolve.mts:191): for a src/bin directory that two binaries declare, every path with super is dropped, also one that stays inside the directory (super::y::T from src/bin/common/x.rs names src/bin/common/y.rs in either binary). The base gave that edge, the branch gives none; two binaries sharing a common directory is an ordinary layout, and acceptance line 2 asks silence only for crate:: paths. Minor (512, src/relations/resolve-path.mts:414 and :427, known limitations to state in the changelog): the patched crate's version is not compared with the requirement, so a patch Cargo leaves unused still gives an edge; workspace exclude and package.workspace are not read, so an excluded nested package takes the upper root's patch (a false edge) and its own patch or a root named by package.workspace is ignored; :626 does not lowercase a github URL as Cargo does. Judged sound: the four changed unit tests are true updates (each old fixture asked a root item of a module no root declared, and each keeps its intent with the declaration added); the p04 case lists the library's own mod edge and still proves no edge leaves tools/build.rs; a module both roots declare gives no root item while module paths still bind, as line 3 and the changelog say; legacy_bench_path, infer_subdirectory, target_path and normalize_build were read at Cargo tag 0.88.0 and the code follows them; source matching of [patch] held for a git dependency against a crates-io patch, an alternative registry, target and dev dependencies, the table form, and renames on either side. Not checked: the heavy corpus tier (zed), the go and dotnet oracles (toolchains absent), and the per-commit red of each test commit (the branch's tests were instead run over the base code: 22 fail there, the named cases among them).

A ProjectReference with ReferenceOutputAssembly=false still passes on the referenced project's own references, and the comment gives the reason 'the restore graph is not told otherwise'. NuGet says the opposite: GetRestoreProjectReferencesTask (and NuGet.targets, which it mirrors) takes a ProjectReference into the restore graph only when ReferenceOutputAssembly is empty or true, and transitive project references come from that graph. Probed on the built reader: T -(false)-> A -> B gives T sight of B; T -> A -(false)-> B -> C gives both A and T sight of C. MSBuild shows neither. This is the same extra reach the issue removes (a name two projects declare reads as ambiguous), one hop further, and no case covers it. Wanted: the reference is not followed and not passed on, with a catalogue case for each of the two shapes, and the comment corrected. | Minor: csharp-reach.mts:288-297, metadata set by an Update item, by an ItemDefinitionGroup default, PrivateAssets=compile, ExcludeAssets=all or IncludeAssets=none is not read. All keep more reach (fail open), the first three are not named in the comment; a known limitation. | Minor: no case shows that a consumer of a project holding a plain Reference does not see the referenced assembly (flows: false at :328); probed by hand, it holds. | Tried against the reader and held: False/FALSE, lower-case element and attribute names, single quotes, attribute before Include, spaces around =, a raw > in another attribute, child element with whitespace and newlines, CDATA (reads as not written), a commented-out child, a Condition on the child, the item, the ItemGroup, a property as the value, a list Include, two items for one project (the wider wins), Directory.Build.props with MSBuildThisFileDirectory and a plain path, PrivateAssets as All, as a child, inside a list, with a second direct reference. | Not checked: the C# oracle (dotnet is not installed here), the heavy corpus tier (jellyfin, eShop), a real MSBuild build of the probes; the NuGet behaviour is read from NuGet's source, not run. - 2026-11-11 11:50 key 20261022T1010-llqr by rev-340-fable · 340 review changes · by rev-340-fable (fresh) · model claude-fable-5-2 · Critical 1, a rule passes over a file it refused before, and yg check says nothing about it (source/cli/src/structure/hook-loader.ts:149-151 and 186-198, source/cli/src/structure/rule-text.ts:35-38). I attacked the built tool two ways. (a) In a copy of examples/no-secrets-in-logs I added src/leak.ts to the payments component: a comment holding one NUL byte, then logger.info("login", password). On release/6.2.0, yg check --approve --only-deterministic prints FAIL with error[refused] no-secret-in-logs at src/leak.ts:4. On the branch it prints "2 passed · 0 refused" and PASS; the only extra line is the relation-file-binary warning, which speaks of dependencies and of no rule. One byte in a comment now switches a script rule off for that file, and this file is 130 bytes, so memory gives no reason to withhold its text. (b) A rule that refuses a marker string, and a 65 MiB src/dump.sql that holds it: release/6.2.0 refuses. The branch keeps the recorded refusal until an unrelated file of the component changes; then --approve --only-deterministic records "2 passed" and yg check prints PASS with no line naming dump.sql. The other direction fails too: a rule that requires an owner line now refuses a file with an early NUL that has the line. Of the 144 check.mjs files in the repository 33 read content and none reads unread, so each of them sees such a file as empty. Under quality-before-convenience the tool has to name the files a rule did not read, or hold the pair back, and it does neither. (+8 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

- 2026-11-11 12:41 key 20261103T0440-fikt by w-509-takeover-fable · 509 evidence · Assumed: the rule is now this. The Rust extractor declares, for every file, each module the file places by name alone (a mod x; item of the parse tree, also inside inline modules, with no path attribute, cfg_attr or attribute macro on it or around it, in a file that parses to the end). The resolver follows these declarations from the asking file up to the roots of its tree. One root reached: it is probed first, the other roots after it in the release branch's order. Two or more reached: a root item binds none. None reached: the release branch's order. A root that is not reached is never ruled out, so the only place where an edge of release/1.1.0 becomes silence is a file that two roots reach by plain chains. This replaces notes 2, 5 and 6: the text reader of root files is removed.
- 2026-11-11 12:41 key 20261103T0440-fikt by w-509-takeover-fable · 509 evidence · Assumed: line 3 holds in its first half only. A module that both roots declare by plain mod gives no root item (case rust-module-of-two-roots-root-item-edge, the old case renamed). A module that no root declares keeps the release branch's edge (new case rust-module-no-root-declares-root-item-edge), because a missing declaration does not show that no crate compiles the file: three review rounds found files placed by a path attribute, include! or a macro in a root or in a file below it. The takeover's direction names a file no parent declares as a gap that gives the base's answer. The acceptance line still says neither gives no edge; it needs the jarl's amendment.

- 2026-11-11 13:03 key 20261103T0440-fikt by rev-509-opus · 509 review changes · by rev-509-opus (fresh) · model claude-opus-5-5 · batch 20261111T1303-wrrn · Important (509, src/relations/extractors/rust.mts:435 INERT_MOD_ATTRIBUTES, read by plainModuleFiles at :448; the silence at src/relations/resolve-path.mts:307): a #[cfg(...)] on a mod, on the inline module around it, or at the head of a file of the chain counts as inert, so a root whose declaration a cfg leaves out counts as certainly compiling the file. Beside the same plain mod in the other root, an edge of release/1.1.0 becomes silence where one root compiles the file. Reproduced on the built tool against release/1.1.0 (a1ef8c4), package with src/lib.rs and src/main.rs, crate::Opts asked from the module: lib.rs #[cfg(any())] mod x; with main.rs mod x; and Opts only in main.rs gave src/main.rs and now gives nothing; the same with #[cfg(feature = "never")] mod x;; lib.rs #[cfg(any())] mod outer { mod x; } with main.rs mod outer; and src/outer.rs mod x; (asked from src/outer/x.rs) the same; the mirror (main.rs #[cfg(any())] mod x;, lib.rs mod x;, Opts in both) lost src/lib.rs. This breaks the property the takeover is judged on (silence only where two roots provably compile the file), and docs/api.md:85, the doc of plainModuleFiles (rust.mts:444) and the changelog say a reached root certainly compiles the file or are silent that cfg counts. A cfg declaration may still order the roots but should not count toward the two that give silence, with a case for each shape; if the jarl reads the tool's blindness to cfg as "two roots in some configuration" and accepts it, it becomes a limitation to state in the changelog and the API doc instead. Important (record, by the tool's rule): no worker row names line 3 of 509 as the jarl amended it at 12:50; the worker's row at 12:48 names the earlier wording and shows the same two cases green at fdeb751, so this is a gap of the record left by the amendment, not missing proof; my row names the current line. Minor (509, src/relations/resolve-path.mts:315, commit fdeb751): the edition of a file is read from the library and src/main.rs even when the one root known to compile it is a [[bin]] declared in src/, while that root is still probed for edition 2015 bare paths: in an edition 2015 package with [[bin]] path = "src/cli.rs" and edition = "2018", src/cli.rs mod foo; mod args; and src/args/mod.rs use foo::Bar; now give src/args/mod.rs:1 -> foo, with or without src/lib.rs, where release/1.1.0 and be4f2fb give none and edition 2018 names an external crate. Reading the edition from the roots known to compile the file, when there are any, would also give the true edge of the mirror shape (2018 package, 2015 [[bin]] in src/), which release/1.1.0 and fdeb751 miss and dafb234 gave. An input hardly anyone gives. Note for the merger, not a finding: the branch conflicts with release/1.1.0 at a1ef8c4 (the C# merge of 500, 504, 528) in docs/api.md, test/relations/catalogue.test.mjs (case count) and test/relations/extractor-rev.test.mjs (neighbouring rev lines). Held on the built tool against release/1.1.0: no silence from a mod written by a macro in a file below a root (one root or both), a #[path] in the middle of a chain (alone, or beside a plain chain from main.rs), include! in one root beside a plain chain from the other, a cfg_attr on a mod, cfg_if!: each gives the release edge or the reached root's. Silence only where two roots reach by plain chains: both roots plain, an inline mod b { mod a; } in one root with mod b; and a b.rs or b/mod.rs declaring mod a; under the other (either way round), a [[bin]] in src/ beside the library, the edition 2015 bench at src/bench.rs beside the library, three roots with two reached, super:: climbing to the root, #[cfg(test)] mod tests { mod fixtures; } in both roots, inert attributes and raw identifiers. Better than release where a chain proves one root: src/main.rs declared as a module of the library (src/x/mod.rs -> bin, src/main/x.rs -> root), a file the library loads by path that is a plain module of main.rs, a deep chain through mod.rs files. The rev 4 to 5 is right: declarations() gains the modfile keys, the repository raises the rev on every change of an extractor's output (docs/api.md:17; Rust went 2 at v1.0.0 to 4 on release/1.1.0, C# 3 to 19), and a table cached at rev 4 lacks the keys, which would leave every src/bin directory without main.rs with no crate. The edition fix restores the a261bc0 shape (util -> helpers on release/1.1.0 and fdeb751, lost at be4f2fb), apart from the Minor. Nothing protective weakened: no test removed; the four refitted unit tests are back as on release/1.1.0; the only removed test lines are the count, the rev line, an import line and two manifest expectations that now also assert git; the takeover commits each name 509, one change each, no amend, no AI trailer. Not checked: the heavy corpus tier (zed), the go and dotnet oracles (toolchains absent), check:dist as the script runs it (the extraction is no git repository; dist compared by diff -r).

On the second merge the post-merge step and yg log merge-resolve --node app exit 1 with log-merge-history-rewritten and say an entry of the recorded history was rewritten. The lock driver kept the baseline of the merge base, and each side holds an older entry before that baseline's last entry, so no side and not the merged log passes the append-only test. The release build verifies the same merge and records the baseline. After the refusal yg check names yg log merge-resolve --node app as the step, every form of it refuses (no sides, HEAD^1 and HEAD^2), and an entry written anyway reads log-integrity prefix_modified until someone commits it. Two branches that each merged an older side branch give the same result. No test merges two sides that both hold an older entry before the base's last one. Minor, CHANGELOG.md:112: the headline says yg log merge-resolve no longer records a baseline over a rewritten log, and the stopped rebase or cherry-pick route still does (filed outside). Minor, source/cli/src/cli/log.ts:473 and :515: the eol advice prints only after a successful merge-resolve, so a repository without the attribute that never runs it gets no advice; the worker said so, and yg check no longer misreads such a log. Minor, CHANGELOG.md:98: a blank line splits the Fixed list before the two new entries. Judged and accepted: the remaining limit of 303. A date-keeping rebase gives a replayed commit and its entry the same dates as a commit written after the rebase, so committed data cannot tell them apart; CHANGELOG.md:99 and docs/the-lock.md:181 state it and their wording covers the order m f f f as well as f m f f. A .cts or .cjs file, an import x = require() and a require() call enter require, and a .mts or .mjs file (static or dynamic import) enters import, under every resolution that reads exports (Bundler, Node16, NodeNext), whatever the preset sets. Probe, 360 comparisons with TypeScript 6.0.3 through the tracked-file view: presets @tsconfig/node18, @tsconfig/strictest and @tsconfig/vite-react; app options {}, moduleResolution bundler, moduleResolution nodenext, module esnext, allowJs; a CommonJS and an ES app; a dual package listing import first and one listing require first; importers .mts static, .cts static, .cts import-equals, .ts import-equals, .js require(), .mts dynamic import. The compiler gives one branch per file kind for every preset, installed or not; 0dc4d75 agreed in 360 of 360, 623040e in 180 (where the first target happens to be the right branch), the same as release/1.1.0. So round 1 brings back, for every config that extends an installed preset, the defect 553 was filed for, and its changelog line (a require() call, an import x = require() and a .cts or .cjs file bind the require branch) is untrue for those configs. The new unit row at :283 pins the wrong answer: app/a.mts must bind lib/cjs/index.cts for seven option sets, among them moduleResolution bundler and nodenext written by the config itself, where the compiler binds lib/esm/index.ts in every case, so a correct fix turns it red. What is really unknown under an unread base: the format of a .ts, .tsx, .js or .jsx file under a static import, whether a dynamic import() is rewritten to require (it depends on module), the node condition (Bundler versus Node) and customConditions. Direction: keep the condition the extension or the call form fixes, bind only when the answer does not depend on what stays unknown (for example the same target with and without node), otherwise the undecided reading; add a compiler comparison row with an installed preset. What round 1 got right stays: a .ts file of a CommonJS app with a require-first package, and the dual dist package that gave silence and a false package-entry-missing at 0dc4d75, now bind as the compiler does (44 probe rows). | Minor (010), Runes src/relations/extractors/typescript-resolve.mts:1344: package-entry-missing still says that no tsconfig of the package maps the entry when two tsconfigs map it to different sources and nothing binds for that reason. Probes: tsconfig.build.json {rootDir src, outDir dist} beside tsconfig.types.json {emitDeclarationOnly, rootDir lib, outDir dist} (tsc --listEmittedFiles: both write dist/index.d.ts), and beside a tsconfig.json that extends @tsconfig/vite-react (an unread noEmit) with rootDir lib and outDir dist. The silence is right, the stated reason is not. Wording, a known limitation. | Checked and holding: red before green at 9ebaec1, tests 286, pass 283, fail 3, the three named failures; at 623040e tests 2244, pass 2243, fail 0, skipped 1, the rebuilt dist identical to the committed one. No golden moved: between 0dc4d75 and 623040e only corpus/explained.md changed under corpus/; the routine gate passes for 25 repositories with 0 added and 0 removed; the heavy tier gives react 10029 and typeorm 11875 edges, 0 added, 0 removed, and jellyfin's 18 unexplained C# edges are the same at the merge-base 691b1a3 (already issue 556). The 76 next-intl entries (76 + entries and 76 typescript:false-edge entries) now say what is true: packages/swc-plugin-extractor declares no dependency, its pnpm lockfile importer is {}, the root depends on no next-intl, so pnpm links next-intl nowhere the fixtures reach and the compiler finds nothing before or after a build, and Runes binds them through the older undeclared-member rule (570). The 3 react entries now name the oracle's limit, and it holds: compiler/ is its own yarn v1 workspace with its own lockfile, outside the root's workspaces, and babel-plugin-react-compiler-rust names dist/ in main and types with a tsconfig from src to dist. No vote: both round 1 probes now bind packages/core/src/index.ts; a solution-style tsconfig with files [] and references, and one holding only .js without allowJs, no longer vote (tsc --listEmittedFiles: they write nothing); a lone noEmit tsconfig gives silence and the report. The message no longer says that imports of the package are not resolved. The [read] line of 010 'Runes side, determinism: the file view (issue 235) lets a consumer resolve against the commit's own files; the consumer halves are in 530 and 143' holds: 120 of 120 probe layouts give one answer through the tracked-file view, and through node_modules and dist excluded, with and without a build on disk and with and without the preset installed. One issue per commit, subjects name the issue, fixes as further commits. Not run: npm run coverage; check:dist (no git checkout, replaced by the dist comparison); the strict corpus with go and dotnet (not installed here). No extractor rev moves, no export is added, the catalogue count is unchanged.

Minor (509, src/relations/extractors/rust.mts:489 attributeIsCfg): an inner cfg_attr is taken to apply a cfg by the text pattern cfg\s*\(, so '#![cfg_attr(all(), cfg /* c */ (any()))]' at the head of src/lib.rs, which empties the library crate, leaves its 'mod x;' certain, and beside 'mod x;' in src/main.rs the release edge src/x.rs:1 -> bin (crate::Opts only in main.rs) becomes silence; an input no one is expected to write, a known limitation. Guard attacked on the built tool with 15 crate roots for `use crate::ensure;`: raw string, doc comment, #[doc] attribute, impl method, const block, macro_rules body, trait item, unknown macro, fn nested in a static initializer stay silent; extern block, use alias, cfg fn, r#ensure, fn after a broken fn, lazy_static item bind. Assumptions: no table keeps the 1.0 text reading (holds); a root extern crate name still binds the root for crate:: and facade paths (holds, as 1.0); the four resolver rows (the input cannot compile, the tree rule binds the binary; no guard weakened); the eight cases given edition 2021 are about manifest tables, pass at base too, and rustc 1.99.1 rejects their use in 2015 (E0432); per-file alias facts (Minor 4); unknown macros lose edges only. Not re-run: coverage. Findings, compared against rustc 1.99.1 in a rust:1-slim container. Important 1 · src/relations/resolve-path.mts:83 and docs/api.md:86: crate:: root items and the root items of a dependency are now read only from the table (base read the root's text). Grain's check path (arch.mjs computeArchHits: hydrateTable(compactDecls(...)) into makeResolver, named in plan-runes) keeps per key only the first file of each of the first two directories, and every module that writes `use core_lib::Engine;` declares item:Engine itself, so the root rarely survives. With Grain's compactDecls copied verbatim: `use core_lib::Engine;` against a root `pub use engine::Engine;` binds core-lib/src/lib.rs at base and silences at the tip; so do crate::Error re-exported by the root, crate::Config in three crates, and edition 2015 util::slug through the roots' extern crate. The full table gives the edge on both. docs/api.md says both consumers need no change; grain check would lose Rust edges into crate roots once it vendors 1.1.0. Needs a decision: the requirement stated in docs/api.md and Grain keeping the Rust per-file keys whole before 6.2.0 ships, or another reading. Minor 2 · src/relations/extractors/rust-resolve.mts:156: the per-file externcrate exemption lets a use path bind the dependency in a file that writes an aliased or nested extern crate of it: root `extern crate util as u; mod util; use util::slug;`, a module with `extern crate util as u; use util::slug;`, or `extern crate util;` in a fn body; rustc names the local module in all three, the tip binds util/src/lib.rs (as base did), against 516 line 1. Minor 3 · rust-resolve.mts:141-147: in edition 2015 the extern crate names of every root are asked before the items of the root that compiles the file: lib.rs `extern crate util;`, main.rs `mod util; mod cli;`, cli.rs `use util::slug;` binds the dependency where rustc names main's module. Minor 4 · rust-resolve.mts:142 with the per-file keys of rust.mts topLevelExternCrates: `extern crate engine_core as core2;` atop src/api.rs and `pub mod inner { pub mod core2 { … } use core2::Engine; }` gives a new false edge src/api.rs:5 -> engine-core/src/lib.rs (base silent); rustc names inner::core2. Minor 5 · src/relations/extractors/rust.mts:548: inside its proc-macro crate the derive function's own name is still a root item: `use crate::builder;` in src/helper.rs compiles, base binds src/lib.rs, the tip is silent (lost edge only). Minor 6 · rust-resolve.mts:156: Yggdrasil declares only mapped files, so in an edition 2015 crate whose root is mapped to no node every path-dependency import of its modules is now silent (bound before); docs/api.md says it only for root items. Minor 7 · docs/api.md:86: the two "Called without the table" sentences read as contradicting each other (2015 dependency paths bind as from 2018, then an edition 2015 use path stays silent). (+1 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

- 2026-11-11 15:24 key 20261111T0927-mdle by w-537-fable · 537 evidence · Assumed: line 1 is met by a private configuration directory per reviewer process, not by a limit. Reason: the Claude CLI reads its configuration file at startup and can write it at any point of its life, so a limit would be safe only at one reviewer at a time on the whole machine, across every repository; a private directory removes the shared file instead. The CLI honours CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (read in the installed CLI 2.1.322 and tried against a scratch directory: a file cut off mid-write there gives 'Claude configuration file at ... is corrupted: JSON Parse error' and a .corrupted backup, exit 1). Credentials are not copied. The CLI finds its credentials store through CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR when set, else through CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so the reviewer sets the first to where the user's sign-in already is (the user's own value, else their CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, else empty, which the CLI reads as its default place and default keychain entry). Tried with 'claude auth status', which calls no model: a private directory alone answers loggedIn false, with the empty variable loggedIn true. A copy was rejected because a token refreshed in a directory that is then removed would leave the user's sign-in stale. The private directory starts from a copy of the user's .claude.json (read only, skipped if it does not parse) and is removed when the call settles or the run is interrupted.
- 2026-11-11 15:24 key 20261111T0927-mdle by w-537-fable · 537 evidence · Assumed: a CLI that cannot find the sign-in from a private directory (one older than CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR) must keep working, so the provider asks 'claude auth status' once per run from a private directory, and on anything but loggedIn true runs every review on the user's own configuration as before. Asking beforehand was chosen over running a failed review a second time because the repository's provider-retry-contract rule forbids a provider retrying after a sign-in failure. No real review was run: a paid call would be needed to prove the full path with the real CLI, so that part rests on the two unpaid probes above and on the stand-in tests.

Six 2-second files took 14 s at 1 and 4 s at 6, so the cap is honoured. Unset and empty give 4; 0, -3, 2.5, abc and true are refused with exit 2 and a message that names the value; " 3 ", 1e2 and 0x10 are accepted as 3, 100 and 16. A failing test gives exit 1, a pass exit 0, and the script works from another directory. It imports only node built-ins. CI calls npm test on Ubuntu and Windows with Node 22 and 24, where node expands the globs itself. README.md and CLAUDE.md name GRAIN_TEST_CONCURRENCY and the default 4, and neither tells an agent to call Grain. The default is honest for a 16 GB machine: 4 files at the measured 1.31 GB each is about 5 GB. Full suite at 4009d0d8 under MemoryMax=12G: 2377 tests, 2364 pass, 7 fail, 6 skipped, 454 s on 2 cores; all 7 failures are in tests/canonical-exemplar.test.mjs, the known ones. Only the four files of the commit moved. Not run: Windows. Minor: the script uses spawnSync and forwards no signal, so SIGTERM sent to it alone ends it with 143 while node --test and its test files keep running (6 processes left in the probe); a time limit that signals the whole process group, as coreutils timeout does, still stops everything. Minor: when node --test is killed by a signal the script exits 1, not the signal's code. Minor: arguments after npm test -- are dropped without a word, so npm test -- <file> runs the whole suite; before the change the file was added to the full list, so it never narrowed. It should narrow, or refuse the argument, as a separate issue. Minor: the 5 GB in README is computed from 4 x 1.3 GB; the measured peak on 2 cores was 2.73 GB. Minor: the script's comment says about 1 GB, the docs 1.3 GB.

It says a file that parses into one very wide node 'is now read in time proportional to its size in every language'. Three languages still slow down with the square of the size on malformed files of the issue's size, and this work changed none of them (same time and same facts on release/1.1.0, 28e52cf). (a) C#: lines '(A a, B b) = ' repeated to 387 996 characters take 24.5 s of C# fact extraction (1.4 s at 97 000, 5.8 s at 194 000, ratio 4.2), past the issue's own 10 s bound. Lines 'new List<(Order Item, int Index)>(' take 6.9 s (ratio 3.5). A CPU profile puts 2.8 of 3.6 s in get parent from declaresVariable (src/relations/extractors/csharp.mts:581-588: decl.parent, arg.parent and tuple.parent over the flat ERROR run, called at :1726). That is the declaration-expression helper the worker left for 577 as 'measured linear', and it is not linear. (b) TypeScript and TSX: lines 'g<import('x').T>(' take 0.48, 1.8 and 7.4 s at 97 000, 194 000 and 388 000 characters. The profile puts 1.37 of 1.6 s in get nextSibling from misreadImportTypes (src/relations/extractors/typescript.mts:269); a sibling read costs what a parent read costs. This is filed outside below. (c) Kotlin: damage recovery (589). '@A.B fun f(' takes 2.6 s at 97 000 and 13.5 s at 194 000; 'val x: A.B<C> = (' takes 31 s at 97 000 and 130 s at 194 000, the time in parseAt. Two fixes would work. Either the sentence names the languages that got faster (Java, Kotlin, PHP, Rust, Ruby, and C# on dotted names) and drops 'in every language', or C# and TypeScript are fixed here. Repro on the built tool: main holds three recorded entries. After git rebase --continue, yg check reports only log-entry-missing; after yg log add and yg check --approve it exits 0, with the rewritten first entry in the log. A cherry-pick of that branch onto main gives the same, and so does a commit that only deletes the last recorded entry. Round 1's module refuses each of these with log-merge-history-rewritten, and yg check stays log-integrity. The rewrite sits one commit before the fork, so the limit of 50 commits plays no part; the worker's report names this gap only beyond 50 commits. The unit case at tests/unit/core/log-merge-refusals.test.ts:260 fixes the skip on the log as it stands, and no test deletes or re-times the last recorded entry before a replay stop. CHANGELOG.md:111 and docs/the-lock.md:153 say the history the branch being built on recorded has to survive, and here it does not. (+10 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

- 2026-11-11 16:05 key 20261002T1239-mnen by w-182-takeover-fable · 182 evidence · Assumed: the invariants a file identity keeps, and the rule built from them. (1) At any commit, two paths present in its tree never hold one identity. (2) A path holds an identity only from the commit that put the file there (an add, a rename, a merge that brings it in) along that commit's first-parent descendants, until a commit on that line deletes it or renames it away; a merge that keeps an old path beside the renamed one gives the path that arrives from the other parent a new identity at the merge itself, whether or not a later commit names both. (3) The identity of a path at a commit is read from that commit's ancestors alone: the nearest commit on its first-parent line that set the path, with a merge read by its difference from its first parent. The order commits are walked in never enters, so a refreshed history equals a cold one at every point and no refresh walks from the root. (4) Every identity has at most one path today and every path at most one identity, so a pair is always between two different paths and a commit counts once per present-day file. Choices the invariants leave open: a path deleted and added again on one line continues the file born there, as the release branch counts it by path, unless that file lives on under another name, and then it is a new file; the same path added on two lines is one file; where a merge has two files for one path the first parent's stays, and where it has one file for two paths the first parent's path keeps the earlier commits.

- 2026-11-11 16:27 key 20261029T1423-mevg by w-363-takeover-fable · 363 evidence · Assumed: the remote is asked with one git setting added for that call alone, a url.<address>.insteadOf rule under which the address of the push stands for itself; it is the longest prefix a rule can name, so it wins over a rule that names a mirror. git ls-remote --get-url confirms the address first; when git would still ask another (a rule that names the whole address, or a remote whose name is the address), the remote is not asked, one line says so and the whole range is read. Chosen over reading the whole range under every rewrite, which would refuse every new branch of a repository with a public name for anyone who fetches through a mirror.
- 2026-11-11 16:27 key 20261029T1423-mevg by w-363-takeover-fable · 363 evidence · Assumed: a merge is read as an ordinary commit against each parent (git's diff of the two blobs), and a name counts when it is new against every parent. So a line with an already public name that a merge moves or repeats is refused, as in an ordinary commit; round 2's reading passed it. A file one side renamed is compared with the file it was, which closes round 3's Minor 7 where git pairs the two files; where it does not, every line counts as added (named in rails/README.md).
- 2026-11-11 16:27 key 20261029T1423-mevg by w-363-takeover-fable · 363 evidence · Assumed: a commit is read from its own bytes in UTF-8 and in the encoding it declares, never through git log; a commit that declares an encoding the scan cannot decode is refused with a line of its own. Bytes that are not UTF-8 with no encoding declared are read as UTF-8, a known limit named in rails/README.md.
- 2026-11-11 16:27 key 20261029T1423-mevg by w-363-takeover-fable · 363 evidence · Assumed: the question to the remote runs under a small watching process, in a process group of its own with no terminal; at 60 seconds, or when the push is interrupted, the whole group is stopped. - 2026-11-11 16:59 key 20261111T1312-tzye by w-574-takeover-fable · 574 evidence · Assumed: round 4, the rule written before the code. The target of a replay is the commit it began on: the commit a rebase replays onto, or HEAD as it stood before a cherry-pick of one commit or of several. At a stop three histories have to survive, entry for entry, in the log about to be recorded. One: the target's log as it stood when the replay began. Two: the version the target's own committed baseline describes; when the target's log still starts with it, it is at hand, otherwise it is read from the target's own history and from nowhere else. Three: the log at the merge base of HEAD and the replayed commit. Only entries that came with the replayed commit's branch may be absent: what its parent held and the target never did. The baseline the lock driver left in the working tree, or in a commit this replay made, is not consulted, so a baseline of the replayed branch cannot stand in for the target's. Out of reach: the target's log does not start with its recorded version and no commit within the walk from the target holds it. That covers the 50-commit limit, the edge of a shallow clone, and a version no commit of the target ever held. Then merge-resolve refuses and says why. In a shallow clone the step is git fetch --unshallow and the same command again; in a full clone it is to abort and settle the log on the target first, by the two-branch form or by restoring the entry. A version found only on the replayed branch is never read as the other branch's. Honest cases that must reconcile: round 1's backport, rebase --onto, a cherry-pick stopped on a source conflict, round 2's rebase onto a fast-forwarded merge, rebase --rebase-merges, autostash, cherry-pick -m, reordered picks in one command and in two, a shallow clone with no rewrite, and a rebase whose earlier step left the replayed branch's baseline in HEAD's commit.

- 2026-11-11 17:26 key 20261002T1239-mnen by w-182-takeover-fable · 182 evidence · Assumed: three choices the invariants leave open, each taken as the release branch counts it or as git names it. A path deleted and added again on one line goes on as the file born there (by path, as release/6.2.0), unless that file lives on under another name. A file a commit deletes is not the file the same commit adds at another path: git would have called that a rename, and counting both as one file would name it twice in that commit. A merge is read against its first parent only, so where it has two files for one path the first parent's stays and the other file's commits from before the merge are left out of today's counts; where it has one file for two paths, the first parent's path keeps the earlier commits (the test of a file renamed two ways now expects c.js 16 and b.js 9, where the rename dated first kept them before).

- 2026-11-11 17:53 key 20261111T0927-mdle by rev-537b-opus · 537 review approve · by rev-537b-opus (fresh) · model claude-opus-5-5 · Minor 1 — the dead-run cleanup can remove a live run's folder (source/cli/src/llm/claude-code.ts:139-158, folder name at :162): a folder counts as a dead run's when its machine tag (a hash of the hostname) is this machine's and process.kill(pid, 0) finds no such process in the cleaner's own process list. Two runs that share a temporary directory and a hostname but not a process list each see the other's folders that way: a sidecar container on another container's network (tried: a container started with --network container:<the dev container> reports the dev container's hostname, and its own shell is process 1), the containers of one Kubernetes pod sharing an emptyDir as the system temporary directory, a --network host container with the host's temporary directory mounted. Reproduced with a stand-in: a folder named with this machine's tag and a process number no local process has, in use by a live stand-in reviewer, was removed by the first review of a local yg check --approve on the same TMPDIR; the reviewer found its stored key gone (ENOENT at its end) and made the folder again on its way out. An API-key user's review in the other container can then start without its key and fail 'Not logged in' (fail-closed, worded as lasting); the user's file is not touched. The comment at :120-124 and the providers log entry say the machine in the name covers containers sharing a temporary directory; it covers only containers with distinct hostnames. A liveness test that does not rest on the process list (an age floor above the longest review timeout, the pid namespace in the name, or a lock the owner holds open) would close it. Minor 2 — in the fallback (a CLI that finds no sign-in from a private folder, so reviews share ~/.claude.json), isTransientFailure (claude-code.ts:224-233) re-reads the user file when the failing reviewer exits, while other reviewers sharing it may be mid-write: with a stand-in whose half-written window is 5 ms, three runs of 10 calls said 'failed on a reviewer fault that passes by itself' twice and 're-running will not help until the connection/config is fixed' once, the file parsing afterwards every time; with a 400 ms window every failure read as lasting. So the older CLIs this fallback serves still get the issue's wrong message under contention, at random. A re-check after the run's reviews end, or a short retry before calling the file broken, would make it stable. Tried and held on the built tip, with a stand-in claude, a scratch HOME and a scratch TMPDIR (no real CLI, no paid call): 10 reviews at once, each saving its configuration half-written for 400 ms — all passed, 10 distinct folders (0700, file 0600) holding only primaryApiKey, the user's file kept its inode, size, mode and mtime; a symlinked, a mode-000, a missing, a half-written, a keyless and a directory-shaped ~/.claude.json — reviews ran, the folder empty where no key could be read, the user's file untouched; CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set (key read from that folder, sign-in pointed there), set empty (treated as unset), CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR named by the user (passed through); SIGTERM and SIGINT mid-review with reviewers that save 600 ms after the signal — the late saves landed while the folders existed, then every folder was removed, no reviewer left, exit by the signal; reviewers that ignore SIGTERM — killed after the 2 s grace, folders removed; SIGKILL mid-review — six folders left, each holding only the key, removed by the next run's first review, and a run started while another was mid-review left all six of the other's folders in place with its reviews intact; SIGHUP — the same leftovers and cleanup as SIGKILL (not caught, as before the change); a sign-in question that ignores SIGTERM — stopped at 30 s, killed at 35 s, the run went on in the fallback, no stray process; in the fallback a file that stays broken keeps the lasting wording and the CLI's advice. Red before: at 77713ccd6 the round-2 tests fail 7 of 16 for the right reasons; the full check is green at the tip. Read in the installed CLI 2.1.322 (not run): with -p, a .claude.json empty but for the key makes it neither prompt nor refuse — onboarding, the trust dialog and the terms dialog are steps of the interactive start only; a key from the environment is used without the approval list in a non-interactive run; the stored key is read from primaryApiKey (saving it to the keychain is switched off in this build); auth status prints JSON unless --text and sets loggedIn from stored credentials, an API key or a third-party provider; the OAuth refresh lock lives in the credentials store folder (CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR, so ~/.claude), so parallel reviewers still take turns refreshing; the macOS keychain entry name follows CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR as the user's own run resolves it (empty means the unsuffixed entry; a named folder hashes to the user's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR suffix). It does behave as on a first start: each review fetches the account profile, feature flags and model-access list itself and keeps none, and what the user's file had cached (an organisation's model default, the model-access list) is not applied from the cache. One narrow consequence: with an OAuth token without the profile scope (setup-token) and no cached model-access list, a request for claude-opus-5 is sent as claude-opus-4-8; the user's own file usually lacks that list for such tokens too. Not proven: a real review end to end (paid), Windows and macOS (read only), the cost of the per-review profile and flag fetches under parallel reviews. Line 1 [read] 'Each reviewer process runs with a private configuration directory, or reviewers started across runs are limited, with the choice and its reason in the issue': met — a private folder per call, seen per call in the stand-in log, with the fallback for a CLI that cannot find the sign-in, and the choice and its reason in the issue notes. Line 2 [test]: red before for the right reason, green at the tip in the whole suite. Round-1 findings 1 to 6 are fixed as the worker describes. Nothing protective weakened: no suppress, no aspect, architecture or config change; the dead-exports allow-list has no net change against the base; the replaced test assertions are stricter. Runs in the dev container were bounded by --max-old-space-size=8192 and the cores the throttle pinned, not by a MemoryMax scope: the container's cgroup is read-only.

- 2026-11-11 18:25 key 20261111T1150-vqto by w-561-fable · 561 evidence · Assumed: 'peak memory outside the heap stays bounded' means the check itself never holds the tree of a large file. The parser needs up to 2 GiB to learn that a tree does not fit, so that memory is spent in a process of its own, one file at a time, and given back when it ends; the test asserts a peak resident size of the check under 1 GiB with three such files (496 MiB measured, about 2 GiB before).
- 2026-11-11 18:25 key 20261111T1150-vqto by w-561-fable · 561 evidence · Assumed: the cause is one for both issues, so one commit carries both. The tree-sitter runtime keeps all trees in one WebAssembly memory of at most 2 GiB, aborts when it cannot grow, and answers every later call on that thread with the same abort (measured: even deleting the parser throws). In 561 two files in flight each held a tree; in 610 one tree needed more than 2 GiB.
- 2026-11-11 18:25 key 20261111T1150-vqto by w-561-fable · 561 evidence · Assumed: the issue's inputs (40 MiB of prose) each parse alone in about 1.2 GiB and failed only together, so the test uses dense valid source instead: 56 MiB files that cannot fit alone, and 24 MiB files that fit one at a time. They fail the same way on the release branch and run in seconds, where 40 MiB of prose takes about 100 s per file.
- 2026-11-11 18:25 key 20261111T1150-vqto by w-561-fable · 561 evidence · Assumed: the threshold for reading a file in a process of its own is 4 MiB of text. A tree takes up to about 48 times its text (40 MiB of source took 1.9 GiB), so a smaller file cannot exhaust the parser alone.
- 2026-11-11 18:25 key 20261111T1541-motj by w-561-fable · 610 evidence · Assumed: 'marked as having no tree with the reason' means file.ast is undefined for that file and the pair ends unverified with a report naming the rule, the file and the reason, as a file over the text limit already does. A long file is first parsed in a process of its own, so the rule's thread keeps a working parser and the other rules are judged. When several smaller trees together exhaust a thread's parser, a worker thread is replaced; on the main thread the later rules that ask for a tree are left unverified naming the file the parser stopped on.
- 2026-11-11 18:25 key 20261111T1150-vqto by w-561-fable · 561 evidence · Assumed: the two new process entry files are left out of coverage the way the worker thread entry already is, because they run only as their own processes from the built bundle; their logic is in modules tested in-process.

The read line 1, '[read] The model file's growth from keeping those keys is measured on jellyfin and a Rust corpus repository and stated in the CHANGELOG if it is noticeable', is met: re-measured with the Runes release/1.1.0 build (44a06cc, the C# package merged; its tree equals the head of jarl/494-csharp-base-classes) in place of the vendored copy, each model built from an empty cache: ripgrep 3fce3b5 677 168 to 696 658 bytes (+2.9 %), jellyfin 305a964 9 558 857 to 9 592 351 (+0.35 %), eShop 913acea 1 355 103 to 1 369 767 (+1.1 %). That is not noticeable, so no growth line is owed. Red before green: with that build the fix's test file fails 5 of 6 on the old compaction and passes 6 of 6 on 5d306526. Whole repositories, every file resolved as check resolves it, the model's table against the full table: ripgrep has 14 edges missing in 12 of 111 files with the old compaction and none with the fix; jellyfin and eShop differ in no edge either way (the 456 dropped usings records change no edge there). One fixture per kind, check against the full pass after the edit is committed: Rust extern: in an edition 2015 crate, an extern crate alias (extern:name=crate), modfile: with lib.rs and main.rs both declaring the module (the old check warned of a cycle through src/lib.rs that the full pass does not have), modfile?: (the old check named src/lib.rs, the full pass src/main.rs); C# usings shared by two files of one folder, a base: record of two partial parts with the same base line, and two same-named file types in one folder with the same base line (the old check missed the FIRST edge to the nested type's module in all three). With the fix all seven give the full pass's edges. Tried to break the shape rule: every declared key of the 33 corpus repositories (up to 4 000 files each) and hand-made names (a TypeScript module named node:fs, a C++ namespace item, Ruby, Python, Go, PHP, Java and Kotlin names, Rust raw identifiers): no plain name is kept whole, only the Rust item:, extern:, modfile: and modfile?: keys and the C# tab records, interface: and internal: keys. Runes reads per file only those (resolve-path.mts declared() with tagged keys; csharp-resolve.mts usings, base:, file-base: and members: by file); the scoped extern:: forms are uses and never declared. Full suite on 5d306526 with the gate's environment: 2238 tests, 2231 pass, 0 fail, 7 skipped. Nothing outside the issue moved; no test or check was weakened. Findings: Minor, plugins/grain/engine/relations.mjs:461-462: a crate root's plain names stay compacted, while Runes docs/api.md asks a compacting consumer to keep every key of every crate-root file; the resolver asks a root only for its tagged keys, so no edge differs (ripgrep and the four Rust fixtures), but the contract is wider than what Grain keeps (filed outside for the Runes docs). Minor, plugins/grain/tests/check-table-whole-keys.test.mjs: with the vendored Runes 1.0.0 the end-to-end check test passes on the old compaction too, and there is no C# end-to-end case; both start to tell the two tables apart only with 143, and since the C# reading is now on release/1.1.0, 143 can add the usings and file-base cases. (+3 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

- 2026-11-11 18:51 key 20261103T0440-ukah by w-514-fable · 518 evidence · Assumed: acceptance line 2 says a first segment that names both a local name and a crate is an error in Rust and gives no edge. rustc 1.x (rust:1-slim, editions 2018 and 2021) compiles it and binds the local name: with a path dependency shapes and a local mod shapes, pub use shapes::Square; resolves to the local module, and the same holds for a name another use bound. So the case rust-edition-2018-use-local-module-over-crate-edge asserts the edge to the local module and none to the crate, not silence. The examiner should judge this line against rustc.

- 2026-11-11 18:51 key 20261103T0440-qytd by w-514-fable · 514 evidence · Assumed: only a glob of a module in the root's own tree is followed, by its path from the root (bare, self:: or crate::). - 2026-11-11 18:51 key 20261103T0440-mtdw by w-514-fable · 522 evidence · Assumed: a file is passed over only where every existing file of the modules above it is known to list all its modules (new key mods:all) and none declares it. A file with an unread macro among its items, an unread inner attribute or a parse error is not known, and the fitting file is bound as before, unless it is another Cargo target's root. Without the pass's table nothing changes, as docs/api.md promises for 1.0 behaviour. Sixteen existing catalogue cases and two unit fixtures used a module no mod declared; each gained the mod line and its edge.

- 2026-11-11 19:14 key 20261103T0440-qytd by rev-514-opus · 514 review approve · by rev-514-opus (fresh) · model claude-opus-5-5 · batch 20261111T1914-jujh · Approve at e762b68, Minor findings only. Re-ran: the full suite (2523 tests, 2522 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped: go not installed), dist fresh, every new case red over release/1.1.0's code, the corpus gate and verify --tier all passed, and every fixture compiled with rustc 1.99.1 (decoys and stale files poisoned with compile_error!, never read). Rev 11 to 18 is one bump per output-changing commit; e762b68 changes no output (uses() and declarations() identical to 03bbf5f over 1001 Rust files). Catalogue 893 = case files = runCase calls. The 109 corpus lines are react's Rust compiler crates (72 for 518, 36 for 514's pub use reactive::*) and ripgrep's crates/index (518), each true in the source. All ten key kinds the extractor declares (mod:, mods:all, glob:, pathmod:, pathmod-name:, item:, extern:, modfile:, modfile?:) match Grain's per-file rule on release/6.2.0, names do not, and a Grain-style compacted table gives the same references as the full one on react and ripgrep. The three limit cases fail when the code is broken for them. 518 line 2: its text is false for rustc 1.99.1, which compiles a local mod shapes beside a dependency shapes with no ambiguity error and binds the local module; the case asserts that edge; the director should restate the line to the compiler's behaviour before merge (no code change). Minor 1, src/relations/resolve-path.mts:92: a name two cfg-exclusive root globs bring in (#[cfg(unix)] pub use unix::*; #[cfg(windows)] pub use windows::*;, both defining Order) gives no edge, and so does one item two globs reach (b re-exports a::Order); rustc compiles both and the edge is the root file either way: a lost edge, never a false one. Minor 2, src/relations/resolve-path.mts:76 and :102: each mods:all question copies the key's whole file list (filesFor(...).includes), and nearly every Rust file declares mods:all, so the check is linear in the Rust files; a synthetic package with stale files went 0.5 to 0.6 s at 2003 files, 1.4 to 3.1 s at 8003, 3.8 to 11.6 s at 16003 (quadratic); react shows no change. Minor 3, reference/relations/rust/rust-path-loaded-file-relative-path-forms-edge.md:21: the fixture does not compile as written: rustc does not collapse imp/.. without a src/imp/ directory, and the wrap mod's path names src/wrap/platform/tty.rs, which is missing; the tty expectation is Runes's rule for a file nothing loads, not a compiler fact. Noted: under the coverage run (99.15/95.70/99.19, above the thresholds) two timing tests of the Go and C# extractors failed on one throttled core; the plain suite passes them.

- 2026-11-11 19:29 key 20261111T1421-uzsy by w-592-fable · 592 evidence · Found outside the twelve issues, for filing (w-592-fable): (1) rails/messages.mjs drops every line of a message that begins with # before it reads it, in a range too, so a private URL or a local path on such a line of a committed message passes the message rail (the names rail reads the whole text). (2) A pushed new ref (a tag, a new branch) makes Althing's own pre-push read the whole history of the pushed commit: about 1,500 commits here at about 1.25 s each, because the 2.3 MB loop log is scanned whole for every commit that touches it (42 commits took 52 s with the old code and with the new); a tag push to Althing would wait about half an hour, and the nightly history scan costs the same. The names range asks the remote what it has instead. (3) A text file in an encoding other than UTF-8 is read as UTF-8, so a name with a non-ASCII letter in it can pass; only a commit's and a tag's own text is refused when it is not UTF-8. (4) What a signature's bytes hold (an X.509 certificate's subject, an OpenPGP signer's user id) is not read. (5) The rail code/read-only-to-tools misses a tag made in the call shapes 613 names for a push (options before the name in an array, the name handed to a helper). (6) yg check prints the word the rule lang/english refuses, at pre-commit and in CI, so a listed name written with a Polish letter is printed there; that rule has no key to know it. (7) In a SHA-256 repository a deletion line of a push (64 zeros) is not read as a deletion by either scan, which compares with 40 zeros; it ends with exit code 2. (8) A refusal line prints a file's path as it is, control characters and line breaks included.
