- 2026-11-11 19:38 key 20261111T1312-tzye by rev-574d-opus · 574 review changes · by rev-574d-opus (fresh) · model claude-opus-5-5 · batch 20261111T1938-xcbv · Important, source/cli/src/core/log/log-merge-resolve.ts:527 to :531 (replayedHistory pushes the raw log at the merge base of HEAD and the replayed commit into the history that has to survive), refused at :550 to :557: a replay stop is refused when the merge base holds text nobody recorded, so the printed way out of a real refusal loops, and the refusal says HEAD lost an entry it holds. Repro on the built tip, round 2's own repro shape followed as printed: main records three entries; one commit on main changes the text of the first (yg check: log-integrity); feature is cut from that commit, changes src/a.ts and adds an entry (committed without the fill, which the rewrite blocks); main changes src/a.ts. git cherry-pick feature stops and yg log merge-resolve --node app refuses, rightly. Then as printed: git cherry-pick --abort, the entry and yg-lock.logs.json restored from the commit before the change, committed (yg check on main: no log-integrity), git cherry-pick feature again: it stops, and merge-resolve exits 1 again with log-merge-history-rewritten, ".yggdrasil/model/app/log.md as HEAD commits it has lost or changed 1 entry of its own history: <the first entry's datetime>", and the same step. HEAD holds that entry exactly as recorded; what the resolution lacks is the rewritten text at the merge base, the rewrite commit, which any branch cut while the rewrite stood has as merge base. Repeating the step changes nothing. git rebase main with main restored gives the same. The build of release/6.2.0 (03ac2699d) reconciles the same stop to main's restored log plus the picked entry, and after the continue yg check asks only for the entry. The way out that works is not printed: resolve the log by hand and continue without merge-resolve; yg check is then clean after the fill. The same hold refuses a second shape in which neither branch is red: main commits an entry before its fill, topic is cut there, adds and fills its own entry, main then corrects the wording of its still unrecorded entry and fills (yg check exits 0 on both); git rebase main and git cherry-pick topic stopping on src/a.ts are refused with "lost or changed 1 entry of its own history" and the step to restore main's draft wording. A two-sided merge of those two branches refuses the same as a clash since 6.1.0, so that shape is arguable; the restore shape is not, since nothing anyone recorded is lost there. The hold came in with d5b4e55cb (round 2) and stayed; no earlier round followed the restore step on a branch cut after the rewrite, and no test does. Holding the merge base's log only as far as its own committed baseline records it would keep every recorded entry and drop both refusals. (+16 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

- 2026-11-11 19:40 key 20261111T1414-swrg by rev-573-opus · 587 review changes · by rev-573-opus (fresh) · model claude-opus-5-5 · batch 20261111T1940-mmlp · Important 1 (631 line 1; the package as it lands): cd0c0fcf merged with release/6.2.0 at 7f5c3ef3 (a clean textual merge, tree cb118b36) is red. plugins/grain/engine/history.mjs is 50590 characters there: release brought it to 49988 (182/217 moved code to lineage.mjs) and 606's guard adds 602 (the try/catch in git() at history.mjs:36, batchOut at :49, started() in gitOk at :54). npm test on the merge: tests 2291, pass 2282, fail 2, skipped 7; the two are tests/engine-module-size-budget.test.mjs and the branch's own tests/own-graph-enforced-rules.test.mjs ('error[refused] engine/file-size-budget, 1 violation in plugin/engine/history'). So 631 line 1 fails on the release tip once this lands, and the oracle README's '1629 passed, 1 refused' is no longer what the check prints. Bring release in and move the guard out of history.mjs (process-start.mjs holds the rest of it) or otherwise bring the module under the budget. On cd0c0fcf alone both tests pass (7 of 7). | Important 2 (605 line 1): EXTR_V is still g37 (engine/config.mjs:7), though 592c2a87's body says 'Needs: EXTR_V'. Probe: a store written by the release code while the Python extractor threw on app/orders.py, read by cd0c0fcf: 2 file edges where a clean index gives 3, no 'dependencies not read' line, and grain refresh and grain refresh --full both print '8 from cache, 0 parsed'. The old entry {s, r: null} has no why, so readAgain (oversize-relations.mjs:145) keeps it as a file in a language without an extractor. Same shape as 169's Minor 3, which was made a condition of that merge and bumped on that branch. | Minor 1 (573, wording): for an over-limit Java file whose read gave no facts, a reference by simple name from its own package is missing from the model (com/x/A.java to com/x/Data.java: 2 edges to Data when read, 1 when unread), while the note says only 'dependencies from it are not resolved ...; 1 dependency to it is counted, from a file that names it by path or package' (report-facts.mjs:204). The old sentence was right about A; the new one no longer says that a dependency to the file by name is not resolved. | Minor 2: export.mjs:210 says the reader of lines at a commit is in history.mjs ('history.mjs has it'), and tests/own-graph-enforced-rules.test.mjs:3 says it comes 'from the history layer'; it is linesAtCommit in grain-export.mjs:17. | Minor 3 (606, by reading): three starts are still outside the guard. measure.mjs:255-259 turns any failure of git rev-parse, EMFILE included, into 'no commit X in this repository', a stop that names no limit and says something false; the history walk's spawn (history.mjs:314 on the merge) has no 'error' listener, so a refused start there is an uncaught crash; grain-check.mjs gitNameOnly and mergeBase rethrow the raw spawn error. Seven commands (status, report, where, check, export with and without anchors, measure) under ulimit -n 24 to 56 never reached them: each run stopped at an earlier guarded start with the ulimit -n message or gave the unlimited answer (export differed only in indexedAt). | Judged and found sound: e661b462 is acceptable. The oracle is a test fixture whose architecture file the loop has kept in step with the code before (486, 591, the 117 and 124 splits); the edit maps CHANGELOG.md, which exists, to repo/config, which the README's node already relates to, and adds one path to that type's when; no rule, scope, status, review_by or suppression changed. Moving the git read out of export.mjs is a real fix, not a dodge: the rule's own description names the dispatcher as a module that may talk to git, grain-export.mjs is mapped to plugin/dispatch (cli-dispatch, 'the ONLY module that may reach git for a query'), and the serializer now takes the reader as an input, so its output is a function of what it is given; the only other caller (grain-advise.mjs:590) passes anchors: false. 605's rule matches 169's: an extractor error is unfinished, kept and named through automatic refreshes, read again by grain refresh, and --full reads every file without facts; measure keeps an end only while the index holds that outcome or the outcome is the file's own, and never one built on a parser failure. Agreement probe (an extractor error, a parser failure and an over-limit file without facts in one repository): status, report, export and measure name the same three files and none gives an edge from them. 612 line 2 [read] holds: 'When grain measure reads an earlier commit's file itself and the read stops, its log line names the next grain measure, as its note does'; measure.mjs:92 passes readAgainBy 'the next grain measure', learn.mjs:90 hands it on, partition.mjs:259 and :281 print it, and the third test of address-space-limit-never-ends-the-run was red on 6ea10bd2 and is green. 631 line 2 [read] holds: 'The stress oracle's graph matches the tree again, or its README says plainly which parts are out of date and why its scores still mean something'; the README's dated paragraph lists mappings, repo/instruments, the director nodes, relations, drill cases and reviewer pairs, and says what a score still means. Guards attacked: ulimit -n 20 to 56 over seven commands; ulimit -v 1.5 to 5.0 GB with one file (four runs each up to 2.2 GB) and 1.6 to 2.4 GB with five files read one after another: no fatal end and no wrong answer on cd0c0fcf, where 6ea10bd2 ended fatally at most of those limits. No added text tells an agent to call Grain. Not run: the full suite on cd0c0fcf alone (the worker's 2250 pass, 0 fail stands; I ran it on the merge), Windows and macOS. - 2026-11-11 19:59 key 20261111T1559-nkyl by rev-620-opus · 615 review changes · by rev-620-opus (fresh) · model claude-opus-5-5 · batch 20261111T1959-icao · Important 1 (627) - a live run's folder is removed by another run in the same container when the temporary directory's path is long: source/cli/src/llm/claude-code.ts:318-327 (holdLock), :332-345 (lockState), :361-365. Node does not refuse a Unix socket path longer than the platform limit (108 bytes on Linux, 104 on macOS); it binds, and connects to, the path cut at that length, so the comment at :292-294 (a path too long for a socket has no lock and only its age speaks) does not hold. (a) A folder path of exactly 108 bytes (TMPDIR of 67 characters with a 7-digit process number) cuts the lock path to the folder itself: listen fails, and another run connecting to a directory gets ECONNREFUSED, reads it as released and removes the live folder. Tried: run A ended Not logged in, 5 passed 1 failed; the release build kept the folder, 6 passed. (b) A TMPDIR of 75 characters or more cuts inside or before the process number, so the folders of different runs share one socket (tried 80: yg-claude-config-<tag>-1). After one SIGKILLed run that socket stays for good (clean-up removes the uncut .lock name, and OWN_FOLDER skips names with a dot), no later run can hold a lock, and every clean-up removes every other live run's folder on the machine. Tried: B removed live A's folder, A failed Not logged in. The release build's process check kept the folder in both. Wanted: never bind or ask a lock whose path the platform would cut (treat that folder by age), or give the lock a short path of fixed length, and a test with a long TMPDIR; a stale cut socket must not keep a host broken. (+11 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

- 2026-11-11 20:00 key 20261111T1312-tzye by w-574-takeover-fable · 574 evidence · Assumed: round 5. At a stop only recorded entries are held from the commit both sides started from: the part of its log its own committed baseline covers, and nothing when it commits no baseline or its log does not start with what that baseline recorded. The version found in the target's history is cut at the baseline's last entry for the same reason. The target's own log as it stood when the replay began is still held whole: a loss there can only come from a commit of the replay itself, and an abort undoes it, so it cannot refuse for good.
- 2026-11-11 20:00 key 20261111T1312-tzye by w-574-takeover-fable · 574 evidence · Assumed: three unit setups that modelled a rewrite with no committed baseline now commit the baseline that recorded the entry first, because text nobody recorded is no longer held. Entries the target still held and a commit of the replay lost get a step of their own (abort and replay again), since there is nothing to restore on the target. The reading of git's record of a stopped replay moved to a file of its own, mapped to the same component, because the reconciliation module had passed the reviewer prompt limit of one rule (97099 characters against 96000).

Important 2: EXTR_V is g38 (config.mjs:7); round 1's probe (a store written by release/6.2.0 while the Python extractor threw on app/orders.py, read by the tip) now extracts again: '0 from cache, 8 parsed', 3 file edges as a clean index gives. Minor 1: the note ends 'one that names only what it declares is missing' (report-facts.mjs:205). Minor 2: both comments name grain-export.mjs. Minor 3: measure's commit lookup, review's merge base and file list and the history walk stop with the limit message; with each guard taken out in a scratch copy its test turns red (measure 1, review 2, walk 1, and without the refresh's throwIfStartRefused the ulimit sweep test). Guards attacked: ulimit -n 24 to 56 over status, report, where, check, export with and without anchors, measure and review: 24 to 38 every command stops naming the limit and prints nothing, 40 to 56 the unlimited answer, never 'no git'. ulimit -v 1.6 to 2.4 GB, 32 runs: exit 0, the file read or named as unfinished, no fatal end (release: 4 of 4 fatal at 1.6 GB). Nothing added tells an agent to call Grain; no assertion was removed. [read] 612 line 2 holds: 'When grain measure reads an earlier commit's file itself and the read stops, its log line names the next grain measure, as its note does' (measure.mjs:93 passes readAgainBy 'the next grain measure', learn.mjs:90 hands it on). [read] 631 line 2 holds: 'The stress oracle's graph matches the tree again, or its README says plainly which parts are out of date and why its scores still mean something'; the README's paragraph lists what is out of date and now carries the merged tree's figures, which I reproduced. | Minor 1 (606, introduced by this round's move of the guard): headSha (history.mjs:39-45) now returns null for a refused start, and only ensureFresh checks for one (grain-context.mjs:245). grain oracle record returns at grain.mjs:84-88, before the end-of-command check at :441, so it records asOf 'unknown' (oracle.mjs:637). Probe with the worker's own stub refusing 'rev-parse HEAD' on the staged Grain tree: cd0c0fcf stops with 'could not start git (EMFILE) ... (ulimit -n)', exit 1; 69a44d09 exits 0 and writes a record with asOf 'unknown', the value for a checkout with no commit. Reaching it needs a refusal at that one start, which the round's own tests treat as possible at any moment. | Minor 2: process-start.mjs:41-46 catFile now holds git's cat-file call, run with a spawnSync the caller hands in, and its comment says 'this module starts nothing itself', which is not true: the process starts from there. engine/no-subprocess-in-analysis-layer passes only because its check reads imports; its own text says to move the work to the module that may spawn or pass the result in. The earlier batchOut(r) took the result; that form in process-start.mjs, with the spawnSync call kept in history.mjs, keeps the module under the budget too. Not run: Windows and macOS. (+1 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

Reaching it needs a refusal at that one start, which the round's own tests treat as possible at any moment. | Minor 2: process-start.mjs:41-46 catFile now holds git's cat-file call, run with a spawnSync the caller hands in, and its comment says 'this module starts nothing itself', which is not true: the process starts from there. engine/no-subprocess-in-analysis-layer passes only because its check reads imports; its own text says to move the work to the module that may spawn or pass the result in. The earlier batchOut(r) took the result; that form in process-start.mjs, with the spawnSync call kept in history.mjs, keeps the module under the budget too. Not run: Windows and macOS. (+1 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

- 2026-11-11 20:17 key 20261111T1331-dfxy by rev-578-fable · 578 review changes · by rev-578-fable (fresh) · model claude-fable-5-2 · batch 20261111T2017-pasd · Important (635): a file that one file declares by name and another loads through a path attribute loses its edge to the first. src/lib.rs writes mod util; and defines Thing, tests/it.rs writes #[path = "../src/util.rs"] mod util; and defines Thing, src/util.rs writes use super::Thing;. rustc 1.99.1 compiles it. release/1.1.0 gives src/util.rs:1 -> src/lib.rs; the tip gives src/util.rs:1 -> tests/it.rs and nothing to the library. The climb takes the path loader as the only parent, while docs/api.md itself says the same file can also be a module by its name; wanted: the declaring file by name counts as a parent too (probed first, or the parent untold), with a catalogue case. Important (614): the worker recorded no proof row, and the catalogue holds no case of the acceptance's form: rust-module-extern-crate-alias-not-in-inline-module-edge writes the alias in src/api.rs, not in the crate root. The behaviour is met: with the alias in src/lib.rs the use inside inner gives no edge on release/1.1.0 and on the tip, compiled under rustc; wanted: that case in the catalogue and the row. Minor (638): the kept answer of a root's globs is renewed only when the name gains files, so a question asked before the root's glob key is declared stays answered 'no' after it is declared (release answers src/lib.rs, the tip nothing); the set kept per key beside it is renewed correctly. Minor (638): the rewritten fixture drops the expectation src/platform/tty.rs:1 -> tty for a comment naming a known limit; the gap is filed as 651. Minor (600): the three older cases moved to edition 2021 keep their expectations and still test the package's own name reaching the library, but none compiles as written (no src/lib.rs for the test crate, no src/cli.rs, a manifest with no target), which 651 covers. Met: 578, 579, 600, 601, 617, 618 and the rest of 638, each new case red on release/1.1.0 for its own reason, green on the tip and compiled under rustc 1.99.1 with and without features; the speed test fails on release (7875 ms against 123888 ms) and passes on the tip in 785 ms; npm run check 2539 tests, 0 fail, dist fresh; corpus gate passed, ripgrep 0 added 0 removed; 904 case files equal the catalogue count; the Rust rev rises once in each of the four commits that change the extractor's output (19 in 60c4819, 20 in 29c7a70, 21 in bdea7f2, 22 in 1c9bc29) and 8d25719 changes none; glob?:<path> fits the whole-key shape ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*\??:(?!:). 634 [read] met: docs/api.md says 'glob?:<path>, like glob:<path> and every other per-file key of these paragraphs, is a key a consumer keeps whole: the word before its one : is lowercase and is no Rust path, so the key is never split at ::, shortened or merged with another', and the paragraphs name item:, extern:, extern:<name>=<crate>, modfile:, modfile?:, mod:, mods:all, pathmod:, pathmod-name:, glob: and glob?:. Tried against the guards: a cfg_attr with a comment, a doc(cfg) and a nested cfg_attr; a local mod in a function body against the alias; three binaries over one src/bin folder; a plain glob beside one under a cfg (edge) and two plain globs (silence). (+1 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

Minor (638): the kept glob answer is renewed only when the name gains files, so a question asked before the root's glob key is declared stays no; the rewritten fixture drops the tty expectation (651). Minor (600): the three cases moved to edition 2021 do not compile as written (651).
- 2026-11-11 20:18 key 20261111T2018-zbqe by rev-549-opus · filed 654 · Runes, C#: a Using item of a project file whose Condition holds a raw > before its Include is not r…
- 2026-11-11 20:18 key 20261111T1034-bgpw by rev-549-opus · 549 review changes · by rev-549-opus (fresh) · model claude-opus-5-5 · batch 20261111T2018-mupl · Changes, one Important finding; every line of the eleven issues is met otherwise. Important (584), src/relations/resolver.mts:362 (takesCall) with docs/api.md:95: whether an extension reading takes a call is read from the shapes: records of the files the table lists under the extension key, and a consumer that keeps only some files of a name key, as docs/api.md allows and Grain release/6.2.0's compactDecls does (one file per directory for a key without a tab or a tag, every shapes: record kept whole), loses the sibling file whose method takes the call. Reproduced with Grain release/6.2.0 and this build in its vendor folder, Grain's own makeEdgeResolver over the full table and over hydrateTable(compactDecls(...)), as grain check reads it: src/ext/A.cs declares Tag(this Order), src/ext/B.cs Tag(this Order, string), src/web/Page.cs calls o.Tag("k"): the full pass gives Page.cs -> src/ext/A.cs, the compacted table nothing; with the base build (a94d31b) both give the edge. jellyfin and eShop differ in no file either way, so the corpus does not show it. docs/api.md:95 tells a consumer to hand these keys to the table like the other keys with a tab, which Grain does, so the documented contract no longer keeps check and the full pass equal (ruling per-file-keys-are-kept-whole). A fix: read the shapes of the bound owner's files from the shapes: records themselves, or name the extension keys among the keys a compacting consumer keeps whole. Minor (595), src/relations/extractors/csharp-resolve.mts:270 (cannotTake) and src/relations/extractors/csharp.mts:1640 (argumentType): two inputs give a new false extension edge, none on the base: a parameter written dynamic is read as a framework type that refuses an enum value (void Log(dynamic v) beside Log(this Lib, Kind): lib.Log(Kind.A) gives src/web/Page.cs:6->ext, C# binds the instance method), and a const field is read as a variable of its type (const int Max = 5 with Set(byte) beside Set(this Lib, int): lib.Set(Max) gives src/web/Page.cs:7->ext, though a constant in range converts to byte, C# spec 10.2.11). Minor (636), test/relations/extractors/wide-node.test.mjs:88: the comment says a name of two segments never reaches the qualified-name parent read, and gives 204 s; with only that read put back on 9eb9987 the two-segment test fails as well (1442 against 23519 ms) and the three-segment one too (2171 against 26707 ms); with only the declaration-list read put back both pass; the commit message says the two-segment input was red too. So the new test does fail for 566's C# change (its qualified-name read) and passes otherwise; the declaration-list read of 566 is still guarded by no test, and 636's premise (the existing tests pass with 566 reverted) does not reproduce here. Minor (628), docs/api.md:89: file-interface:<key> is read for its own file alone (csharp-resolve.mts isInterface, filesFor(...).includes(file)), but the paragraph names only the keys with a tab as those a consumer keeps under every file; Grain keeps it by its shape, so nothing breaks today. enum: and converts: are read with has() and need no file list; shapes: is named at :95. What I tried against the new refusals (rule try-to-break-a-guard), each as a catalogue-shaped case through the case runner on both builds: an enum parameter nested in a base class (no false edge), a dynamic parameter (false edge, above), a const argument (false edge, above), params ReadOnlySpan<object> (no false edge), an argument whose class implements the parameter's interface through its base (no false edge), this._config.Get(key) with the field in another part and no instance Get (edge kept) and with the field in a repository base that has Get (silence), a compilation-unit alias Data against a nearer namespace App.Data (App.Data wins on the branch, the alias on the base), an internal partial type whose project grants the caller its internals beside a public type (silence, as the compiler is ambiguous). Checked and holding: the 13 new catalogue cases all fail on a94d31b for their issue's reason and pass on 9eb9987; the reach tests of 552 and 559 fail on a94d31b; full suite 2512 tests, 2511 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped, rebuilt dist identical to the committed one; corpus gate --tier all passed (jellyfin 32133, eShop 2017, CleanArchitecture 452, every other repository unchanged; the C# oracles skipped, no dotnet here). jellyfin golden: 447cc91 removes 516 lines and adds none, and I read all 516 calls against their target's extension methods: every one passes a count none of them takes (Contains with one argument against Contains(this IEnumerable<string>, ReadOnlySpan<char>, StringComparison) 328+, FirstOrDefault with a predicate 91+, Count() 32, Split with 2 or 3 arguments 18+, IndexOf with 2 or 3, SetImagePath with 3, CopyTo with 4, GetImagePath with 2, GetItemById<BaseItem>(id) against a non-generic extension, GetAllArtists(x) against one of no argument); a9912e8 adds 9, all read: a string id beside ILibraryManager.GetItemById(Guid) (5) or ImageType.Primary/Thumb/Backdrop beside IImageProcessor overloads that take none (4), all true. Grain release/6.2.0 with each build dropped in, grain refresh from an empty cache: ambiguous jellyfin 179 and 179, eShop 24 and 24 (Grain passes no reach), the per-file maps identical; eShop edges identical; the 475 fewer reference groups on jellyfin are the inner readings of constant patterns (ExtraRuleType.Filename =>), now read once as the whole name. New keys shapes:, enum:, converts:, file-interface: all match /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*\??:(?!:)/ (Grain's jellyfin model holds shapes: 370 and enum: 138 as tagged keys). No new export name: takes, argTypes, fileReceivers, own and CsharpArgType are fields and a type reached through TargetHint, all described in docs/api.md, which the plan allows for a field; the exports test passes. rev 30 to 36, one bump each in e0ddd65, 447cc91, a9912e8, 2136343, 273856b, 75221a8; a965a49 (a comment in csharp.mts), 38615a3 and 2bafe8b (reach), 406c682 and 9eb9987 change no extract: 577's facts hash the same per file on jellyfin, eShop and CleanArchitecture between e0ddd65 and 406c682, and 9eb9987's one-pass search finds exactly what isFileLocalReading found. 577's tuple tests fail on e0ddd65 (1485 against 25464 ms, 464 against 6181) and pass after; its extension-block and primary-constructor tests pass on e0ddd65 too, guards rather than proof. Catalogue 882 = 882 case files = 882 runCase. Declared keys of jellyfin 1.187 to 1.405 MB, extract +2.9 % (jellyfin) and +2.5 % (eShop), as reported. For the merger: release/1.1.0 moved to e9509e1 after the branch merged a94d31b (the Rust package, catalogue 893), so the count lines and corpus/explained.md need joining. (+1 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

- 2026-11-11 20:18 key 20261111T1325-iuem by rev-549-opus · 577 review changes · by rev-549-opus (fresh) · model claude-opus-5-5 · batch 20261111T2018-mupl · Changes, one Important finding; every line of the eleven issues is met otherwise. Important (584), src/relations/resolver.mts:362 (takesCall) with docs/api.md:95: whether an extension reading takes a call is read from the shapes: records of the files the table lists under the extension key, and a consumer that keeps only some files of a name key, as docs/api.md allows and Grain release/6.2.0's compactDecls does (one file per directory for a key without a tab or a tag, every shapes: record kept whole), loses the sibling file whose method takes the call. Reproduced with Grain release/6.2.0 and this build in its vendor folder, Grain's own makeEdgeResolver over the full table and over hydrateTable(compactDecls(...)), as grain check reads it: src/ext/A.cs declares Tag(this Order), src/ext/B.cs Tag(this Order, string), src/web/Page.cs calls o.Tag("k"): the full pass gives Page.cs -> src/ext/A.cs, the compacted table nothing; with the base build (a94d31b) both give the edge. jellyfin and eShop differ in no file either way, so the corpus does not show it. docs/api.md:95 tells a consumer to hand these keys to the table like the other keys with a tab, which Grain does, so the documented contract no longer keeps check and the full pass equal (ruling per-file-keys-are-kept-whole). A fix: read the shapes of the bound owner's files from the shapes: records themselves, or name the extension keys among the keys a compacting consumer keeps whole. Minor (595), src/relations/extractors/csharp-resolve.mts:270 (cannotTake) and src/relations/extractors/csharp.mts:1640 (argumentType): two inputs give a new false extension edge, none on the base: a parameter written dynamic is read as a framework type that refuses an enum value (void Log(dynamic v) beside Log(this Lib, Kind): lib.Log(Kind.A) gives src/web/Page.cs:6->ext, C# binds the instance method), and a const field is read as a variable of its type (const int Max = 5 with Set(byte) beside Set(this Lib, int): lib.Set(Max) gives src/web/Page.cs:7->ext, though a constant in range converts to byte, C# spec 10.2.11). Minor (636), test/relations/extractors/wide-node.test.mjs:88: the comment says a name of two segments never reaches the qualified-name parent read, and gives 204 s; with only that read put back on 9eb9987 the two-segment test fails as well (1442 against 23519 ms) and the three-segment one too (2171 against 26707 ms); with only the declaration-list read put back both pass; the commit message says the two-segment input was red too. So the new test does fail for 566's C# change (its qualified-name read) and passes otherwise; the declaration-list read of 566 is still guarded by no test, and 636's premise (the existing tests pass with 566 reverted) does not reproduce here. Minor (628), docs/api.md:89: file-interface:<key> is read for its own file alone (csharp-resolve.mts isInterface, filesFor(...).includes(file)), but the paragraph names only the keys with a tab as those a consumer keeps under every file; Grain keeps it by its shape, so nothing breaks today. enum: and converts: are read with has() and need no file list; shapes: is named at :95. What I tried against the new refusals (rule try-to-break-a-guard), each as a catalogue-shaped case through the case runner on both builds: an enum parameter nested in a base class (no false edge), a dynamic parameter (false edge, above), a const argument (false edge, above), params ReadOnlySpan<object> (no false edge), an argument whose class implements the parameter's interface through its base (no false edge), this._config.Get(key) with the field in another part and no instance Get (edge kept) and with the field in a repository base that has Get (silence), a compilation-unit alias Data against a nearer namespace App.Data (App.Data wins on the branch, the alias on the base), an internal partial type whose project grants the caller its internals beside a public type (silence, as the compiler is ambiguous). Checked and holding: the 13 new catalogue cases all fail on a94d31b for their issue's reason and pass on 9eb9987; the reach tests of 552 and 559 fail on a94d31b; full suite 2512 tests, 2511 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped, rebuilt dist identical to the committed one; corpus gate --tier all passed (jellyfin 32133, eShop 2017, CleanArchitecture 452, every other repository unchanged; the C# oracles skipped, no dotnet here). jellyfin golden: 447cc91 removes 516 lines and adds none, and I read all 516 calls against their target's extension methods: every one passes a count none of them takes (Contains with one argument against Contains(this IEnumerable<string>, ReadOnlySpan<char>, StringComparison) 328+, FirstOrDefault with a predicate 91+, Count() 32, Split with 2 or 3 arguments 18+, IndexOf with 2 or 3, SetImagePath with 3, CopyTo with 4, GetImagePath with 2, GetItemById<BaseItem>(id) against a non-generic extension, GetAllArtists(x) against one of no argument); a9912e8 adds 9, all read: a string id beside ILibraryManager.GetItemById(Guid) (5) or ImageType.Primary/Thumb/Backdrop beside IImageProcessor overloads that take none (4), all true. Grain release/6.2.0 with each build dropped in, grain refresh from an empty cache: ambiguous jellyfin 179 and 179, eShop 24 and 24 (Grain passes no reach), the per-file maps identical; eShop edges identical; the 475 fewer reference groups on jellyfin are the inner readings of constant patterns (ExtraRuleType.Filename =>), now read once as the whole name. New keys shapes:, enum:, converts:, file-interface: all match /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*\??:(?!:)/ (Grain's jellyfin model holds shapes: 370 and enum: 138 as tagged keys). No new export name: takes, argTypes, fileReceivers, own and CsharpArgType are fields and a type reached through TargetHint, all described in docs/api.md, which the plan allows for a field; the exports test passes. rev 30 to 36, one bump each in e0ddd65, 447cc91, a9912e8, 2136343, 273856b, 75221a8; a965a49 (a comment in csharp.mts), 38615a3 and 2bafe8b (reach), 406c682 and 9eb9987 change no extract: 577's facts hash the same per file on jellyfin, eShop and CleanArchitecture between e0ddd65 and 406c682, and 9eb9987's one-pass search finds exactly what isFileLocalReading found. 577's tuple tests fail on e0ddd65 (1485 against 25464 ms, 464 against 6181) and pass after; its extension-block and primary-constructor tests pass on e0ddd65 too, guards rather than proof. Catalogue 882 = 882 case files = 882 runCase. Declared keys of jellyfin 1.187 to 1.405 MB, extract +2.9 % (jellyfin) and +2.5 % (eShop), as reported. For the merger: release/1.1.0 moved to e9509e1 after the branch merged a94d31b (the Rust package, catalogue 893), so the count lines and corpus/explained.md need joining. (+1 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

Reproduced with Grain release/6.2.0 and this build in its vendor folder, Grain's own makeEdgeResolver over the full table and over hydrateTable(compactDecls(...)), as grain check reads it: src/ext/A.cs declares Tag(this Order), src/ext/B.cs Tag(this Order, string), src/web/Page.cs calls o.Tag("k"): the full pass gives Page.cs -> src/ext/A.cs, the compacted table nothing; with the base build (a94d31b) both give the edge. jellyfin and eShop differ in no file either way, so the corpus does not show it. docs/api.md:95 tells a consumer to hand these keys to the table like the other keys with a tab, which Grain does, so the documented contract no longer keeps check and the full pass equal (ruling per-file-keys-are-kept-whole). A fix: read the shapes of the bound owner's files from the shapes: records themselves, or name the extension keys among the keys a compacting consumer keeps whole. Minor (595), src/relations/extractors/csharp-resolve.mts:270 (cannotTake) and src/relations/extractors/csharp.mts:1640 (argumentType): two inputs give a new false extension edge, none on the base: a parameter written dynamic is read as a framework type that refuses an enum value (void Log(dynamic v) beside Log(this Lib, Kind): lib.Log(Kind.A) gives src/web/Page.cs:6->ext, C# binds the instance method), and a const field is read as a variable of its type (const int Max = 5 with Set(byte) beside Set(this Lib, int): lib.Set(Max) gives src/web/Page.cs:7->ext, though a constant in range converts to byte, C# spec 10.2.11). Minor (636), test/relations/extractors/wide-node.test.mjs:88: the comment says a name of two segments never reaches the qualified-name parent read, and gives 204 s; with only that read put back on 9eb9987 the two-segment test fails as well (1442 against 23519 ms) and the three-segment one too (2171 against 26707 ms); with only the declaration-list read put back both pass; the commit message says the two-segment input was red too. So the new test does fail for 566's C# change (its qualified-name read) and passes otherwise; the declaration-list read of 566 is still guarded by no test, and 636's premise (the existing tests pass with 566 reverted) does not reproduce here. Minor (628), docs/api.md:89: file-interface:<key> is read for its own file alone (csharp-resolve.mts isInterface, filesFor(...).includes(file)), but the paragraph names only the keys with a tab as those a consumer keeps under every file; Grain keeps it by its shape, so nothing breaks today. enum: and converts: are read with has() and need no file list; shapes: is named at :95. What I tried against the new refusals (rule try-to-break-a-guard), each as a catalogue-shaped case through the case runner on both builds: an enum parameter nested in a base class (no false edge), a dynamic parameter (false edge, above), a const argument (false edge, above), params ReadOnlySpan<object> (no false edge), an argument whose class implements the parameter's interface through its base (no false edge), this._config.Get(key) with the field in another part and no instance Get (edge kept) and with the field in a repository base that has Get (silence), a compilation-unit alias Data against a nearer namespace App.Data (App.Data wins on the branch, the alias on the base), an internal partial type whose project grants the caller its internals beside a public type (silence, as the compiler is ambiguous). Checked and holding: the 13 new catalogue cases all fail on a94d31b for their issue's reason and pass on 9eb9987; the reach tests of 552 and 559 fail on a94d31b; full suite 2512 tests, 2511 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped, rebuilt dist identical to the committed one; corpus gate --tier all passed (jellyfin 32133, eShop 2017, CleanArchitecture 452, every other repository unchanged; the C# oracles skipped, no dotnet here). jellyfin golden: 447cc91 removes 516 lines and adds none, and I read all 516 calls against their target's extension methods: every one passes a count none of them takes (Contains with one argument against Contains(this IEnumerable<string>, ReadOnlySpan<char>, StringComparison) 328+, FirstOrDefault with a predicate 91+, Count() 32, Split with 2 or 3 arguments 18+, IndexOf with 2 or 3, SetImagePath with 3, CopyTo with 4, GetImagePath with 2, GetItemById<BaseItem>(id) against a non-generic extension, GetAllArtists(x) against one of no argument); a9912e8 adds 9, all read: a string id beside ILibraryManager.GetItemById(Guid) (5) or ImageType.Primary/Thumb/Backdrop beside IImageProcessor overloads that take none (4), all true. Grain release/6.2.0 with each build dropped in, grain refresh from an empty cache: ambiguous jellyfin 179 and 179, eShop 24 and 24 (Grain passes no reach), the per-file maps identical; eShop edges identical; the 475 fewer reference groups on jellyfin are the inner readings of constant patterns (ExtraRuleType.Filename =>), now read once as the whole name. New keys shapes:, enum:, converts:, file-interface: all match /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*\??:(?!:)/ (Grain's jellyfin model holds shapes: 370 and enum: 138 as tagged keys). No new export name: takes, argTypes, fileReceivers, own and CsharpArgType are fields and a type reached through TargetHint, all described in docs/api.md, which the plan allows for a field; the exports test passes. rev 30 to 36, one bump each in e0ddd65, 447cc91, a9912e8, 2136343, 273856b, 75221a8; a965a49 (a comment in csharp.mts), 38615a3 and 2bafe8b (reach), 406c682 and 9eb9987 change no extract: 577's facts hash the same per file on jellyfin, eShop and CleanArchitecture between e0ddd65 and 406c682, and 9eb9987's one-pass search finds exactly what isFileLocalReading found. 577's tuple tests fail on e0ddd65 (1485 against 25464 ms, 464 against 6181) and pass after; its extension-block and primary-constructor tests pass on e0ddd65 too, guards rather than proof. Catalogue 882 = 882 case files = 882 runCase. Declared keys of jellyfin 1.187 to 1.405 MB, extract +2.9 % (jellyfin) and +2.5 % (eShop), as reported. For the merger: release/1.1.0 moved to e9509e1 after the branch merged a94d31b (the Rust package, catalogue 893), so the count lines and corpus/explained.md need joining. (+1 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

- 2026-11-11 20:26 key 20261111T1150-vqto by rev-561-opus · 561 review changes · by rev-561-opus (fresh) · model claude-opus-5-5 · batch 20261111T2026-gixd · Verdict changes. Reruns: the new e2e file is 4 red on release/6.2.0 at 03ac2699d for the right reasons and 4 green on the branch; the 8 touched test files pass (55); scripts/repo-check.sh is fully green (10655 tests, coverage 97.57/96.56/96.96/91.42, Graph: check PASS); yg check --approve --only-deterministic on the repository itself gives the same report with the release and the branch binary, byte-identical dependency facts for all 1297 files and byte-identical script verdicts. The issue's own 561 repro (two .ts of 40 MiB prose, two of binary, max-old-space-size 512) no longer aborts on release at 03ac2699d (binary skipped, prose read; same report on both; peak 1670 MiB release, 385 MiB branch, child 858 MiB), so the switch to dense source in the test is right. The 610 repro (rule reading file.ast of a dense 64 MiB JSON array) now leaves the pair unverified naming src/rates.json and the reason. One file at a time holds in the relation pass: 24 files of 3.9 MiB pass at peak 1048 MiB where release ends error[internal]. 20 files of 4.1 MiB each in its own process: 55 s, no crash (release crashes); cached rerun 0.7 s. Findings: (1) Important, error[internal] still reachable in the default configuration: yg check --approve with a reviewer rule whose companion parses 16 TypeScript files of 3.9 MiB of a uses-related node (none over 4 MiB, a mock reviewer) ends 'error[internal]: Unexpected error while running check: Aborted()'. Stack: Tree.delete in runes destroyParseCache from releaseParseCacheBucket (core/parse-cache-buckets.ts:67) in verifyPairs (core/verify-lock.ts:248): after the companion's parse aborted, the bucket's trees are deleted on the aborted runtime. Release crashes the same way, but the branch's companion handling (structure/hook-loader.ts:825-830) is undone by this and acceptance 561 says never error[internal]. (2) Important, after any abort on the main thread every later parse in the process is refused (ast/parse-guard.ts:105, 114), and the relation pass that runs after the fill (coverage.type_level off, the default) reports every source file as relation-parse-failed 'the parser ran out of memory', naming a small hand-written file and advising to exclude or split it, so following the advice takes source out of the check. Shown with rules on the main thread (YG_DET_TASK_TIMEOUT_MS=0, a documented switch): 20 dense JSON files of 3.9 MiB read by a rule give 'Could not read the dependencies of 3 TypeScript files, e.g. src/charge.ts'; release reports the relations correctly on that run (measured: after an abort caused by accumulated trees, deleting them and parsing again works), so this is a regression there; 16 TypeScript files of 3.9 MiB give the same false report for all 19 files. The 4 MiB threshold does not bound one file either: 64 KiB of TypeScript text 'a<b,' repeated makes the trial process exit out of memory alone (32 KiB fits); in the relation pass it is parsed on the main thread and the other files are reported unread, so a real undeclared dependency beside it goes unreported (acceptance 561: the other files are checked). The comment at ast/parse-guard.ts:15 ('up to about fifty times its text') is not a bound: dense JSON takes about 130 to 175 times. (3) Important, the per-check budget no longer bounds a rule that reads a file over 4 MiB: the trial runs under spawnSync with no timeout (ast/parse-guard.ts:93) inside the worker thread, which worker.terminate() (structure/det-worker-pool.ts:219) cannot interrupt, and the pool's destroy waits for it. With YG_DET_TASK_TIMEOUT_MS=5000 and a rule reading a 20 MiB prose .ts, release stops the rule at 5 s; the branch reports it stopped at 5 s but the fill continues only at 39 s (whole run 109 s against 72 s). (4) Minor, the helper processes are not killed or reaped when the check alone is signalled: SIGTERM or SIGINT to the yg process exits it at once (143, 130) and leaves facts-child running as an orphan for 69 s, and parse-probe-child for 39 s, each able to hold up to the parser's 2 GiB (relations/file-facts.ts:53 and ast/parse-guard.ts:93 are not tied to the interrupt handling the reviewers have); SIGINT to the process group (Ctrl-C) stops both. Release has no such process. (5) Minor, when trees of several medium files accumulate in one rule's bucket, the report names the file the parser stopped on (src/data/m-04.json, 3.9 MiB) as very large or very dense and advises leaving it out, which only moves the failure to the next file; wording, a known limitation. (6) Minor, a file over 4 MiB that fits is parsed twice in the rule path, once in the trial and once on the thread: a rule reading a 24 MiB dense .ts fills in 12 s against 6 s on release. (7) Minor, expectNoIssue(doc, { code: 'check-failed-to-run' }) in tests/e2e/parser-memory.test.ts passes on release too (that cause is a field of an unverified issue, not an issue code), so it proves nothing. Assumptions: 'bounded' as the check never holding a large file's tree holds for the relation pass, not for trees accumulated in a rule's or companion's bucket; one commit for both issues accepted (one mechanism); dense source instead of prose accepted and needed; the 4 MiB threshold rejected as a bound (finding 2); the two process entries out of coverage accepted (det-worker precedent, spawned by the e2e tests); no failing-test-first commit accepted (red reproduced here); the 610 reading met for the pair's own report, with the heading and cause filed outside. Not run: yg drill on a parser-memory file; memory caps could not be applied, the dev container has no memory limit and its processes are outside the host's systemd scopes. (+2 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

Important: after a crash in the main process every later parse in the run is refused (parse-guard.ts:105, :114), so the dependency check reports small hand-written files as out of memory (release reads them); the 4 MiB threshold does not bound a file (64 KiB of a<b, exhausts the parser); the fifty-times comment is not a bound (dense JSON 130-175 times). Important: the trial parse (parse-guard.ts:93) runs synchronously in the worker with no timeout, so a 5 s rule limit moves on only at 39 s. Minor: helper processes outlive a SIGTERM/SIGINT of the check alone (69 s, 39 s, up to 2 GiB each); the report blames the medium file it stopped on; a file over 4 MiB that fits is parsed twice; one test assertion passes on release too.

Not yet true: note-4 says the CHANGELOG states the parse cost of garbage input as a limit, but neither CHANGELOG.md nor README.md mentions it; ruling D10 (a) gives that sentence to the final pass. Measured here on random printable text with 5% newlines, the grammar's own parse: JavaScript 2.3 s for 250 000 characters and 8.1 s for 1 000 000, C# 0.8 and 3.2 s, Rust 0.6 and 2.5 s, Python 0.5 and 1.9 s, Java 0.4 and 1.8 s. A proposed sentence in the CHANGELOG's register: 'A file that is not source code in its language parses in time that grows with its size; a consumer caps the size of the files it reads and skips binaries.'

'Proved' is a structural check, and the exclusion is wider than the README says: any armor in any header line, and anywhere in a tag's text, not only at its end. Only a deliberate forgery reaches it (no accidental path found), so a known limit: narrow the exclusion to where git writes a signature (the gpgsig and gpgsig-sha256 header, the trailing armor of a tag and of a mergetag) and name the forgery in the README's known limits. True SSH- and OpenPGP-signed commits and a signed tag pass clean. Judged on request: Althing's pre-push reads only the commits the pushed refs reach. This checkout sets no push refspec and no mirror; 916 commits are reached only by the local refs/t3 checkpoints and none from a branch, and a new-tag scan of main (648 commits) is clean, so the 290 history refusals cannot block a real push of a branch or tag. A push that carried those refs (--mirror, refs/t3/*) is read and refused by the path and English rails, as it must be. No names refusal is hidden: each prints on its own line, and the nightly runs on a fresh CI clone without those refs. Every leak of the 363 rounds re-run through Althing's own hooks with real commits and pushes to a local bare remote, each refused at the right place with nothing arrived: quoted paths (space, Polish letter, quotes), lines after '++ ' and '+++ b/', merge resolutions that remove a line or join two, a merge adding a file, a split name, author e-mail, committer name, extra header, mergetag, tag message, tagger, tag name, a tag of a tag, raw ISO-8859-2 commit and tag, ISO-8859-2 under an encoding header, an unknown encoding, a replacement object, a graft file (exit 2); a comment-only graft file and true signatures pass. The rails' README says what each scan reads and how'. Tried on the built tool through Althing's own pre-push: an OpenPGP armor with no checksum line, one packet of tag 2 whose length matches, its base64 spelling a test entry on a line of its own; a commit's gpgsig header with it arrived (range clean), and so did a tag whose message holds it in the middle, between prose lines, with a two-word entry written as Kelby/Fenn+A in base64 letters (the test list, not the real one); git shows that text as the tag's message. 'Proved' is a structural check, and the exclusion is wider than the README says: any armor in any header line, and anywhere in a tag's text, not only at its end. Only a deliberate forgery reaches it (no accidental path found), so a known limit: narrow the exclusion to where git writes a signature (the gpgsig and gpgsig-sha256 header, the trailing armor of a tag and of a mergetag) and name the forgery in the README's known limits. True SSH- and OpenPGP-signed commits and a signed tag pass clean. Judged on request: Althing's pre-push reads only the commits the pushed refs reach. A push that carried those refs (--mirror, refs/t3/*) is read and refused by the path and English rails, as it must be. No names refusal is hidden: each prints on its own line, and the nightly runs on a fresh CI clone without those refs. Every leak of the 363 rounds re-run through Althing's own hooks with real commits and pushes to a local bare remote, each refused at the right place with nothing arrived: quoted paths (space, Polish letter, quotes), lines after '++ ' and '+++ b/', merge resolutions that remove a line or join two, a merge adding a file, a split name, author e-mail, committer name, extra header, mergetag, tag message, tagger, tag name, a tag of a tag, raw ISO-8859-2 commit and tag, ISO-8859-2 under an encoding header, an unknown encoding, a replacement object, a graft file (exit 2); a comment-only graft file and true signatures pass. Red before green reproduced for 592/609/616 (11 of 13 fail at df39a35), 622 (3 of 54 at 481812c), 603 (2 of 15 at 83df69c) and 613 (3 of 17 at 3ee9975, failing on git -C <dir> push, not on a missing module). 593 [read] met: method/boundary.md says the names rail 'also reads the pushed range of another family repository, on the maintainer's machine: node workspace/ws.mjs names runs it over a range of that repository's checkout, and the pre-push hook template a tool repository installs (workspace/hooks/pre-push) runs it before a push leaves. The rails' README says what each scan reads and how'. No test, rail or hook weakened; the rule change carries the owner's ratification (code-read-only-to-tools-v2-ratified); rails/english.mjs keeps its old check under english-rule-link-fault-stays. 'Proved' is a structural check, and the exclusion is wider than the README says: any armor in any header line, and anywhere in a tag's text, not only at its end. Only a deliberate forgery reaches it (no accidental path found), so a known limit: narrow the exclusion to where git writes a signature (the gpgsig and gpgsig-sha256 header, the trailing armor of a tag and of a mergetag) and name the forgery in the README's known limits. True SSH- and OpenPGP-signed commits and a signed tag pass clean. Judged on request: Althing's pre-push reads only the commits the pushed refs reach. This checkout sets no push refspec and no mirror; 916 commits are reached only by the local refs/t3 checkpoints and none from a branch, and a new-tag scan of main (648 commits) is clean, so the 290 history refusals cannot block a real push of a branch or tag. A push that carried those refs (--mirror, refs/t3/*) is read and refused by the path and English rails, as it must be. No names refusal is hidden: each prints on its own line, and the nightly runs on a fresh CI clone without those refs. Every leak of the 363 rounds re-run through Althing's own hooks with real commits and pushes to a local bare remote, each refused at the right place with nothing arrived: quoted paths (space, Polish letter, quotes), lines after '++ ' and '+++ b/', merge resolutions that remove a line or join two, a merge adding a file, a split name, author e-mail, committer name, extra header, mergetag, tag message, tagger, tag name, a tag of a tag, raw ISO-8859-2 commit and tag, ISO-8859-2 under an encoding header, an unknown encoding, a replacement object, a graft file (exit 2); a comment-only graft file and true signatures pass. Red before green reproduced for 592/609/616 (11 of 13 fail at df39a35), 622 (3 of 54 at 481812c), 603 (2 of 15 at 83df69c) and 613 (3 of 17 at 3ee9975, failing on git -C <dir> push, not on a missing module). 593 [read] met: method/boundary.md says the names rail 'also reads the pushed range of another family repository, on the maintainer's machine: node workspace/ws.mjs names runs it over a range of that repository's checkout, and the pre-push hook template a tool repository installs (workspace/hooks/pre-push) runs it before a push leaves. The rails' README says what each scan reads and how'. No test, rail or hook weakened; the rule change carries the owner's ratification (code-read-only-to-tools-v2-ratified); rails/english.mjs keeps its old check under english-rule-link-fault-stays. (+2 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

Repro on the built tip: a component svc is created on feature with its first entry and a fill; the next commit changes that entry's text with no fill (yg check on feature: log-integrity); a third commit changes notes.txt and adds an entry; main changes notes.txt. git rebase main replays the first two commits with no stop and stops at the third on notes.txt. yg log merge-resolve --node svc exits 0 with "Log baseline updated". After the continue, yg log add and a fill, yg check exits 0 with the rewritten first entry first in the log. That is line 1's own case, a committed rewrite of the first entry, with yg check green after the continue. The same happens with the component app and the branch's own entry, by rebase and by git cherry-pick of the three commits, and with the entry deleted instead of reworded: merge-resolve exits 0 each time and only log-entry-missing is left. git merge main on the same feature refuses with log-merge-history-rewritten. Rounds 1 to 3 (1e0aa4d58, 58cef27c1, 77a0892d6) and 052118ba0 refuse each of these stops, leave the baseline file unchanged, and keep yg check red. 95a79ddc4, round 4's first commit, lets them through, and so does the release build. No test rewrites an entry on the replayed branch: every replay-stop case rewrites on the branch being built on. The fix has to hold what the replayed branch recorded and the replay carries, while round 1's backport and rebase --onto, which carry only part of it, stay reconciled. (+18 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

Minor 2 (627, wording): the changelog says the lock works however deep the temporary directory is; that holds on Linux only. On macOS a lock name over 103 bytes is not used, so in a temporary directory deeper than about 57 characters a killed run's folder stays up to a day (macOS's default temporary directory is well short of that). Round 1's findings are met otherwise. 627: on 9cc402504 with the tip's test the 67-character case fails (Not logged in) and the 80-character one leaves the cut socket yg-claude-config-<tag>-1; on the tip both pass. A macOS stand-in (process.platform darwin on Linux): a lock at a 103-byte name, none at 104; with no lock a live folder and a fresh dead one are kept and the dead one goes once 25 hours old; at a short path the lock decides as on Linux. 625: a sh wrapper running a node child that ignores SIGTERM and SIGINT: check --approve, aspect-test --node and drill each end after 12s with 'claude --version' did not finish within 10s, and the child is gone; on 9cc402504 the wrapper test's child stays running. Nothing carrying the test runs' TMPDIR survived the touched files (24 files, 286 tests). Every test line re-run and passing on the tip. Judged: the open handle on the temporary directory is opened with close-on-exec and closed when the lock is let go or answered; the socket is unlinked before the handle is closed; Windows goes back to the process list. 620's changelog now speaks of aspect-unknown-key only. Not run: real macOS, Windows. The memory caps could not reach the runs inside the dev container (docker exec leaves the scope). (+1 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

- 2026-11-11 21:15 key 20261111T1312-tzye by w-574-takeover-fable · 574 evidence · Assumed: round 6. What the replayed branch recorded and the replay carries is read from the commits the replay itself made since its target, each as far as its own committed baseline covers its own log. Those commits are always at hand and hold only what the replay carried, so a backport and rebase --onto hold nothing extra. Not covered, by choice: a commit whose log does not start with what its own baseline recorded holds nothing, so a recording commit and a rewriting commit squashed into one by an interactive rebase pass. Searching the replayed branch's history for that case would hold entries the replay does not carry and refuse a backport whose first stop was carried on by hand.
- 2026-11-11 21:15 key 20261111T1312-tzye by w-574-takeover-fable · 574 evidence · Assumed: the step for a loss the replay itself made is to restore the entry in the commit that changed it (git rebase -i, edit, amend), then replay again. A restoring commit at the end of the replayed branch comes after the stop, so it would be refused again. The readers of a committed log and of its baseline moved to the replay file, which leaves the reconciliation module at about 78 200 bytes.

- 2026-11-11 21:35 key 20261111T1150-vqto by w-561-fable · 561 evidence · Assumed: the round-1 design is replaced, not patched. Measured on the real runtime: after one file exhausts it alone, releasing the parse and deleting the parser free nothing and no tree is built again; after trees pile up, releasing the half-built parse lets it build again; a fresh copy of the runtime can be loaded outside the module cache and the dead copy's 2 GiB is collected (eight deaths in a row stay at 2.1 GiB resident). So a stopped runtime is replaced at the next grammar load, and the trial parse in a process of its own is removed: that answers the time-limit finding and the double parse, since nothing is tried first any more.
- 2026-11-11 21:35 key 20261111T1150-vqto by w-561-fable · 561 evidence · Assumed: with other trees held, the report cannot tell a file too dense on its own from trees that piled up, so it states both facts (the file's size, how many trees and how many characters of source the run held) and gives both ways out. A synchronous tree request after the parser stopped, inside the same run, is refused naming the file it stopped on; a different run that only met the stopped parser is run once more on a fresh one.

- 2026-11-11 21:48 key 20261005T1413-fbpi by rev-557-opus · 231 review changes · by rev-557-opus (fresh) · model claude-opus-5-5 · batch 20261111T2148-hwlq · Important 1 (231 line 1): with a graph, a declaring file that no node maps is an owner of its own (relations.mjs:351, ownerKey gives it its directory under a marked key), while yg check reads only node-owned and type-covered files and never declares from it (Yggdrasil relations/pass.ts, enumerateFileRecords and buildSymbolTable). So grain measure and grain check disagree with yg check on a graph that leaves one declaring file unmapped. Probes against the gate's yg: (a) Kotlin import com.x.*, A.kt in node core, B.kt of the same package in no node, app/Late.kt uses A: yg check refuses Late.kt:3 → core; release/6.2.0 gives app→core undeclared and check's first crossing to src/x/A.kt; 69b1de56 gives 0 node dependencies, 1 unresolved reference and no crossing, a dependency yg refuses that release found and the branch loses. (b) C# partial class Money over src/Core/Money.cs (node core) and src/Misc/MoneyOps.cs (no node): yg check refuses Late.cs:7 → core; the branch, like release, leaves 2 references unresolved and finds no dependency. That is 231's own symptom (grain measure shows 0 dependencies where yg check refuses) on a graph that covers part of a repository, which is common. A file no node maps and no type covers should take no part in the node-decided choice, as in Yggdrasil. | Important 2 (644 line 1): grain check names a file whose dependency read threw only when a partition covers it. checkFile returns relUnread with no partition (check.mjs:61-73), and cmdCheck's no-partition branch (grain-check.mjs:310-343) prints the architecture findings, text and --json, without it. Probe: a repository with no source partition, a new tools/new.ts importing ../docs/site.css; extractor working: '[grain] architecture: your import of docs/site.css (line 1) is the FIRST edge tools → docs'; extractor throwing (the test's stub): only 'check tools/new.ts: no partition covers this file', --json architecture [] and only the no-partition disclosure. The file is checked as having no dependencies and nothing says so, in the branch where the architecture finding is all check reports. | Minor 1 (637): identity by equal content at birth splits one file born twice with different content (lineage.mjs:45 idFor, :166 born). Probe: a branch adds u.js and edits it with q.js six times, main squash-merges it, edits u.js with p.js six times, then the branch is merged: release one file (14 commits, q.js 7, p.js 6); the branch two, main's (7 commits, q.js 1, p.js 6) is today's u.js and the branch's 7 commits drop out of today's view. A backport cherry-pick of a later state or an add/add merge does the same. The changelog says it ('the same content added on both branches is still one file'); record it as a known limitation, or decide sameness by similarity as git's rename detection does. | Minor 2 (231, wording): with a graph, measure says references were 'left unresolved, because the name they use is declared in more than one directory' (measure.mjs:370; propose-report.mjs:84 and the comment at relations.mjs:390 alike) also for a name in two nodes of one directory: A.kt and B.kt both in src/x, mapped by left and right, print 'declared in more than one directory: 1 → 1'. 231's changelog says only that missing dependencies appear; some also disappear (two nodes sharing a directory: release drew app→left, the branch none, the worker's own shared fixture too). | Minor 3 (231, by reading, not probed): the index reads the working tree's graph (arch.mjs:303) but is rebuilt only when HEAD moves, and relDecls keeps one declaring file per index-time owner (arch.mjs:324, compactDecls); after an uncommitted graph edit that splits an owner, check (arch.mjs:142, the current graph) sees one declarer and draws an edge yg check calls ambiguous until HEAD moves. The worker disclosed the staleness. | Minor 4 (563): the check now refuses what is counted, and a string-named ambient module is counted as a type: release refused Window, ce, gen of a .ts file's six counted names, the branch all six, among them 'foo' of declare module 'foo' {} (propose-checks.mjs:217). A type-name rule over a partition whose mined .ts files hold one augmentation (declare module 'fastify' {...}) now refuses every declare module '...' in its scope, .d.ts files too; the cause is the count, filed outside. | Minor 5 (wording): history.mjs:284 names the failed command by args.at(-4), which for mergeOps' arguments is '-r' ('git -r failed'); the HIST_V and MODEL_V notes date the change 2026-11-12 (config.mjs:8-9). | Judged sound: 557 uses the shared currentPathOf, which also stops at a path live today, as the other evaluation in evals.mjs does. 563's alias choice: the check refuses the declarations the rule was counted over, as the method rule does (issue 003); counting aliases is an extraction change that moves every TypeScript repository's measure and needs its own evidence; an alias that breaks the rule passes, which the count never claimed. 640's oracle edit: Grain has no graph at its root; the stress oracle is the hand-written answer key the loop keeps in step with the tree (its README's dated entries, the 117 and 124 splits, 631); measure.mjs holds cmdMeasure and commit-tree.mjs is used only by grain-context.mjs, so the query surface is a truthful home; both when changes are described in the README entry; no rule, status or threshold moved. If section 6 of AGENTS.md is read as reaching a fixture's yg-architecture.yaml, it is a ratification for the owner, not a change. 564, 643, 652 met; 567 met by the worker's five suites and mine (2331 pass, 0 fail, 7 skipped). Without a graph release and branch agree on all seven of my 231 fixtures. Guards attacked: ulimit -n 16 to 128 over grain oracle record (never a record without remote or commit); ulimit -v 1.0 to 3.6 GB over grain status (always named); the extractor stub on a file no partition covers (got past: Important 2); the type check over unusual declarations; 231 on graphs with an unmapped file (got past: Important 1). No assertion removed or weakened; nothing tells an agent to call Grain; each issue lands as test then fix with its number in the subject. Not run: Windows, macOS, symfony and kubernetes (a synthetic history of 80 merges stands in for the memory claim). (+2 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

(b) C# partial class Money over src/Core/Money.cs (node core) and src/Misc/MoneyOps.cs (no node): yg check refuses Late.cs:7 → core; the branch, like release, leaves 2 references unresolved and finds no dependency. That is 231's own symptom (grain measure shows 0 dependencies where yg check refuses) on a graph that covers part of a repository, which is common. A file no node maps and no type covers should take no part in the node-decided choice, as in Yggdrasil. | Important 2 (644 line 1): grain check names a file whose dependency read threw only when a partition covers it. checkFile returns relUnread with no partition (check.mjs:61-73), and cmdCheck's no-partition branch (grain-check.mjs:310-343) prints the architecture findings, text and --json, without it. Probe: a repository with no source partition, a new tools/new.ts importing ../docs/site.css; extractor working: '[grain] architecture: your import of docs/site.css (line 1) is the FIRST edge tools → docs'; extractor throwing (the test's stub): only 'check tools/new.ts: no partition covers this file', --json architecture [] and only the no-partition disclosure. The file is checked as having no dependencies and nothing says so, in the branch where the architecture finding is all check reports. | Minor 1 (637): identity by equal content at birth splits one file born twice with different content (lineage.mjs:45 idFor, :166 born). Probe: a branch adds u.js and edits it with q.js six times, main squash-merges it, edits u.js with p.js six times, then the branch is merged: release one file (14 commits, q.js 7, p.js 6); the branch two, main's (7 commits, q.js 1, p.js 6) is today's u.js and the branch's 7 commits drop out of today's view. A backport cherry-pick of a later state or an add/add merge does the same. The changelog says it ('the same content added on both branches is still one file'); record it as a known limitation, or decide sameness by similarity as git's rename detection does. | Minor 2 (231, wording): with a graph, measure says references were 'left unresolved, because the name they use is declared in more than one directory' (measure.mjs:370; propose-report.mjs:84 and the comment at relations.mjs:390 alike) also for a name in two nodes of one directory: A.kt and B.kt both in src/x, mapped by left and right, print 'declared in more than one directory: 1 → 1'. 231's changelog says only that missing dependencies appear; some also disappear (two nodes sharing a directory: release drew app→left, the branch none, the worker's own shared fixture too). | Minor 3 (231, by reading, not probed): the index reads the working tree's graph (arch.mjs:303) but is rebuilt only when HEAD moves, and relDecls keeps one declaring file per index-time owner (arch.mjs:324, compactDecls); after an uncommitted graph edit that splits an owner, check (arch.mjs:142, the current graph) sees one declarer and draws an edge yg check calls ambiguous until HEAD moves. The worker disclosed the staleness. | Minor 4 (563): the check now refuses what is counted, and a string-named ambient module is counted as a type: release refused Window, ce, gen of a .ts file's six counted names, the branch all six, among them 'foo' of declare module 'foo' {} (propose-checks.mjs:217). A type-name rule over a partition whose mined .ts files hold one augmentation (declare module 'fastify' {...}) now refuses every declare module '...' in its scope, .d.ts files too; the cause is the count, filed outside. | Minor 5 (wording): history.mjs:284 names the failed command by args.at(-4), which for mergeOps' arguments is '-r' ('git -r failed'); the HIST_V and MODEL_V notes date the change 2026-11-12 (config.mjs:8-9). | Judged sound: 557 uses the shared currentPathOf, which also stops at a path live today, as the other evaluation in evals.mjs does. 563's alias choice: the check refuses the declarations the rule was counted over, as the method rule does (issue 003); counting aliases is an extraction change that moves every TypeScript repository's measure and needs its own evidence; an alias that breaks the rule passes, which the count never claimed. 640's oracle edit: Grain has no graph at its root; the stress oracle is the hand-written answer key the loop keeps in step with the tree (its README's dated entries, the 117 and 124 splits, 631); measure.mjs holds cmdMeasure and commit-tree.mjs is used only by grain-context.mjs, so the query surface is a truthful home; both when changes are described in the README entry; no rule, status or threshold moved. If section 6 of AGENTS.md is read as reaching a fixture's yg-architecture.yaml, it is a ratification for the owner, not a change. 564, 643, 652 met; 567 met by the worker's five suites and mine (2331 pass, 0 fail, 7 skipped). Without a graph release and branch agree on all seven of my 231 fixtures. Guards attacked: ulimit -n 16 to 128 over grain oracle record (never a record without remote or commit); ulimit -v 1.0 to 3.6 GB over grain status (always named); the extractor stub on a file no partition covers (got past: Important 2); the type check over unusual declarations; 231 on graphs with an unmapped file (got past: Important 1). No assertion removed or weakened; nothing tells an agent to call Grain; each issue lands as test then fix with its number in the subject. Not run: Windows, macOS, symfony and kubernetes (a synthetic history of 80 merges stands in for the memory claim). (+2 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

- 2026-11-11 22:04 key 20261111T1312-tzye by rev-574f-opus · 574 review changes · by rev-574f-opus (fresh) · model claude-opus-5-5 · batch 20261111T2204-tvdf · Important, source/cli/src/core/log/log-replay-stop.ts:98 to :107 (recordedByReplay holds a replay commit's entries only as far as that commit's own baseline covers its own log; recordedEntries at :80 gives nothing when it does not), read at log-merge-resolve.ts:485: when the rewrite of an entry the replayed branch recorded is folded into the commit that recorded it, no commit of the replay holds the entry, and merge-resolve records a baseline over the rewrite at a later stop. Repro on the built tip: feature creates svc with its first entry and a fill, then an unrelated commit, then rewords svc's first entry with no fill, then changes notes.txt, which main changes too. (a) git rebase -i makes the rewording commit a fixup of the recording one, and yg check on feature reads log-integrity; git rebase main stops on notes.txt; yg log merge-resolve --node svc exits 0 with 'Log baseline updated'; after the continue yg check shows only log-entry-missing, and after the entries and a fill it is green with the rewritten first entry. git merge main refuses the same branch with log-merge-history-rewritten, and round 3's build (77a0892d6) refuses the same stop and keeps yg check red; e1175f574 and the tip let it through. (b) The same fixup inside the one git rebase -i main that stops later: exit 0 on every build, 77a0892d6 and release/6.2.0 included. (c) edit on the recording commit in git rebase -i main, the entry reworded and git commit --amend at the pause, a later stop: exit 0. Without a stop the same rebases leave yg check red, so whether the rewrite reads green depends on whether the rebase happens to stop, and git commit --fixup with rebase --autosquash is an everyday way to tidy a branch. This is the worker's first assumption, and I do not accept it as stated: its cost, refusing a backport whose first stop was carried on by hand, is not forced. Round 3's build refuses (a) and reconciles a backport of two commits from main whose first stop was resolved by hand and continued without merge-resolve (second stop exit 0, only log-entry-missing after); the tip reconciles that backport too. In (a) the version the squashed commit's baseline was recorded from is in no commit at all, which is what the merge form refuses on; in (b) and (c) the recording commit is listed in the rebase's own record of the commits it has replayed, and what each listed commit added and recorded is what the replay carries. If the owner accepts the limit instead, docs/the-lock.md:153 and CHANGELOG.md:123 have to name it: today they say an entry one replayed commit recorded and a later one reworded or dropped is refused at the next stop, with no exception. (+12 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

The branch refuses every rewrite of the log made in separate commits, where the release build refuses none. One shape still gets through: an entry reworded inside the very commit that recorded it (a fixup squashed with git rebase -i, or an amend at an edit pause), when a later rebase happens to stop on a conflict. Without a stop the same branch stays red. Options: (1) merge it as it stands, write this shape and the git revert case into docs/the-lock.md and the CHANGELOG as known limits, and file the shape for the next release; (2) one more round, using git's own record of the commits a rebase has already replayed, as the reviewer suggests, with the risk of another round after it; (3) defer the whole guard to the next release and ship 6.2.0 without it.

Controls: without the second declaration, or with it in a folder no type covers, yg refuses Late -> core and the tip agrees. Star and wildcard imports and Go packages agree with yg on type-covered files (the package path drops an ownerless file, as Yggdrasil's does). | Important 2 (665 line 1): plugins/grain/engine/extract.mjs:363 drops every name that opens with a quote or a backtick from the name-shape facts (/^["'`]/, types and methods alike), while the rendered check skips only a quote (plugins/grain/engine/propose-checks.mjs:270, /^["']/), so a Kotlin or Scala name in backticks is refused by a check whose count never measured it, against 665's own 'check refuses only what the count measured'. End to end (partitionLattice, buildAspects, the rendered check, as tests/name-shape-rust-struct-literal-end-to-end does): 16 Kotlin test classes, each with one camelCase helper and one backticked test: release and 69b1de56 count 32 methods at share 0.5 and propose no method-name rule; 60343e6f counts 16 at share 1 with 0 deviants, renders a camelCase check, and it refuses all 16 backticked tests. A backticked Kotlin class is likewise not counted and refused. 665's changelog does not say that backticked Kotlin and Scala names and quoted JS/TS method names leave the method and type counts. | Minor 1 (664 changelog): the change also moves Go packages (and Kotlin star imports): a Go package with a.go in node left and b.go in node right: yg nothing, release and 69b1de56 app -> left with a first crossing, tip nothing; a.go in no node and b.go in core: yg refuses main.go:3 -> core, release and 69b1de56 bind a.go, tip -> core. The tip agrees with yg in both; the changelog names only Java. | Minor 2 (563 changelog): the check reads the counted node types in every language, not only TypeScript: from release to the tip the type check newly refuses a C# struct and C# enum members, a Rust enum variant, a PHP trait, and a Scala object, trait and enum (release's Scala type check refused nothing), and stops refusing a Rust type alias. Count and check now agree there (names that break the shape), the right direction, but 'Can turn a repository red: an abstract class or namespace' understates it. | Minor 3 (wording): plugins/grain/engine/grain-context.mjs:250 still says 'Worktree edits never trigger a rebuild', untrue now that an uncommitted graph edit rebuilds the index; d97b9ec0 carries the round 1 version-note dates of 231 and 637 inside 665's commit. | Closed from round 1, red on 69b1de56 and green on 60343e6f: Important 1 (round 1's Kotlin star import with B.kt in no node, same or another folder, and the C# partial class over a mapped and an unmapped folder: yg refuses -> core, 69b1de56 found nothing, the tip finds app -> core; two nodes in one folder (C#, Java), one node over two folders and nested nodes agree with yg too); Important 2 (644: with no partition, text and --json carry the note and the dependencies-not-read disclosure); Minor 2 ('declared in more than one node: 2 -> 2' with a graph, changelog says some dependencies disappear); Minor 3 (one node split into two uncommitted: 69b1de56 kept a first crossing yg no longer refuses, the tip re-indexes and agrees both ways); Minor 4 via 665 (declare module 'foo', "dq", 'fastify' in a .d.ts neither counted nor refused; Java enum constants likewise); Minor 5 ('git diff-tree failed', red on its test commit 35f20f31 with 'git -r failed'; notes dated 2026-11-11); 637's squash-merge split stands as ruling grain-637-squash-merge-known-limit and the changelog says it. MODEL_V needs no further move: measure snapshots carry the extractor stamp, which moved g38 -> g39 this round, m40 stores re-learn, and a store without a graph signature is stale wherever a graph exists. | Checked and sound: the full suite on 60343e6f from a scratch clone, tests 2353, pass 2346, fail 0, skipped 7, exit 0, 358 s, placement-moves passes, no 'Security violation' (an archive extraction cannot run it: the vendored-code check refuses a folder that is not a git repository); 30 named tests of round 1 and 2 pass with YG_BIN. The commit tree the index reads is always a temporary directory (commit-tree.mjs withCommitTree), so laying the working copy's graph over it never touches the user's files; measure reads each commit's own graph at each end. Round 2 changes no existing test and adds six; each issue lands test then fix with its number; nothing tells an agent to call Grain; no AI attribution. Guards attacked: the graph signature (uncommitted split and merge of nodes, held); type-covered declarers (got past: Important 1); quoted and backticked names (got past: Important 2); Go packages and Java wildcards with unmapped and type-covered files (held). Not run: Windows, macOS. (+1 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)
