- 2026-11-11 22:40 key 20261111T1150-vqto by rev-561b-opus · 561 review changes · by rev-561b-opus (fresh) · model claude-opus-5-5 · batch 20261111T2240-apit · Reruns: the touched test files pass on the branch at ea4c572eb (48 files, 628 tests). The branch's e2e file fails 7 of 7 on release/6.2.0 at 03ac2699d, each for its reason. scripts/repo-check.sh passes every step: 10666 tests, coverage 97.58/96.56/96.97/91.43, Graph: check PASS with 8285 pairs; the two Portal steps ran in the dev container, 67 passed. Round 1's three Importants hold on the tip. The companion over 16 files of 3.9 MiB ends in its own report, with no error[internal] and no reviewer call. With rules on the main thread and 20 dense JSON files of 3.9 MiB, the dependency check still finds the undeclared dependency and reports no small file. With a 5 s rule limit and a 20 MiB prose file, the fill moves on at 5 s, as on release. New shapes that hold: three rules sharing one worker, and the same on the main thread, where one file kills the parser: each rule is reported for its own file and the other component is judged. Twenty small files that kill the parser in a row peak at 2.4 GiB. Trees built after a pile-up are identical to a fresh parser's (10579 nodes, same shape hash). TypeScript, C# and Vue files of 5 MiB read in the helper process give the same findings and byte-identical stored facts as release. SIGKILL, SIGINT or SIGTERM to yg alone stops the helper within 60 ms. No bare Aborted() line appears in any branch output. Findings. (1) Important: yg check with no flag still ends in error[internal] when a file the parser has no memory for is a subject of a reviewer rule. The prompt-size gate resolves yg-suppress ranges by parsing every subject (core/verify-lock.ts:459, then structure/suppress-ranges.ts:60, withParsedFile), and only SuppressMarkerError is caught there, so the ParserMemoryError escapes. Repro: a component mapping src/data/ with a per-file reviewer rule, and src/data/dense.ts holding 'a<b,' 16384 times (64 KiB). yg check prints "error[internal]: Unexpected error while running check: the parser ran out of memory on 'src/data/dense.ts'" and exits 1 after 1.7 s, right after the relation check reported the same file correctly. A 56 MiB generated TypeScript bundle in its place ends the same way after 20 s, with the main process at 2.3 GiB. yg check --approve (core/review-package.ts:215) and yg aspect-test --aspect <rule> --node data (cli/aspect-test.ts:764) end in the same error[internal], and yg drill makes the same call (core/drill-runner.ts:568). Release fails here too: an uncaught RuntimeError Aborted() for the 56 MiB file, and for the 64 KiB file it spins at full processor use after six Aborted() lines (stopped at 600 s). Acceptance 561 says never error[internal], and the CHANGELOG says yg check reads every other file when one is too large or too dense. Neither holds for a component that has a reviewer rule. (2) Important: when reviewer pairs run side by side (parallel above 1; yg init writes parallel: 4 for a command-line provider), one run's parser failure is reported for every other run in flight, naming a file of another component. reportingParserMemory (ast/parser.ts:175-191) takes the first failure after its mark from one record per thread (ast/parse-guard.ts:56 and 70-71), so a failure a concurrent run records becomes this run's report. The count of held trees (ast/parser.ts:69-70) is per thread too. Repro: the e2e-parse-cache-buckets fixture with reads-target-2 attached to gamma, parallel: 10, both companions parsing every target file and returning one small file, and beta and delta each holding 8 dense TypeScript files of 3.9 MiB, so each set fits the parser alone and both together do not. yg check --approve with a mock reviewer passes the one-at-a-time gate stage; the fill then runs both rules together and leaves all 9 pairs unverified, with 0 reviewer calls. Rule reads-target reads only beta, yet it is reported as "Rule 'reads-target' asked for the syntax tree of 'src/delta/q5.ts' (3993626 characters) while its run held 16 other syntax trees", with advice to leave src/delta/q5.ts out of what it judges. Release ends that run in error[internal] Aborted(). The design says a run is never reported for a file that is not its own. Its unit test (tests/unit/ast/parser-memory.test.ts:166) fakes the other run with an abort that records no failure, so it cannot fail for this. (3) Minor: the measurement the design rests on does not reproduce. The message of commit b684ca606 and the cli/ast/runtime log entry of 2026-11-11T21:11 say a parser exhausted by one file never builds a tree again and keeps its 2 GiB. On this branch's runtime, after 'a<b,' 16384 times aborts alone, reset() on the same parser builds the reference tree identical to a fresh runtime's, and so does a new parser after deleting the old one. Only the same parser without reset() aborts again. Replacing the runtime stays correct, but the component's log records a false fact as the reason for the design. Assumptions judged: round 1's design replaced rather than patched, accepted. The report stating the trees held and the file's size with both ways out, accepted for one run on a thread; across concurrent runs it is wrong (finding 2). The signal test skipped on Windows, accepted: the helper notices its parent through the IPC channel closing, which Windows has. Beside this issue: issue 656's shape (two dense JSON arrays of 6.8 MiB walked with descendantsOfType) now reads "The parser ran out of memory while rule 'walks' read the syntax trees it was given", with no Aborted() and no blame on check.mjs; only the heading that 655 covers remains, so 656 may be met by this branch. Memory caps came from a sibling container of the dev image (8 GiB or 12 GiB), since the dev container itself has no limit. (+2 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

Acceptance 561 says never error[internal], and the CHANGELOG says yg check reads every other file when one is too large or too dense. Neither holds for a component that has a reviewer rule. (2) Important: when reviewer pairs run side by side (parallel above 1; yg init writes parallel: 4 for a command-line provider), one run's parser failure is reported for every other run in flight, naming a file of another component. reportingParserMemory (ast/parser.ts:175-191) takes the first failure after its mark from one record per thread (ast/parse-guard.ts:56 and 70-71), so a failure a concurrent run records becomes this run's report. The count of held trees (ast/parser.ts:69-70) is per thread too. Repro: the e2e-parse-cache-buckets fixture with reads-target-2 attached to gamma, parallel: 10, both companions parsing every target file and returning one small file, and beta and delta each holding 8 dense TypeScript files of 3.9 MiB, so each set fits the parser alone and both together do not. yg check --approve with a mock reviewer passes the one-at-a-time gate stage; the fill then runs both rules together and leaves all 9 pairs unverified, with 0 reviewer calls. Rule reads-target reads only beta, yet it is reported as "Rule 'reads-target' asked for the syntax tree of 'src/delta/q5.ts' (3993626 characters) while its run held 16 other syntax trees", with advice to leave src/delta/q5.ts out of what it judges. Release ends that run in error[internal] Aborted(). The design says a run is never reported for a file that is not its own. Its unit test (tests/unit/ast/parser-memory.test.ts:166) fakes the other run with an abort that records no failure, so it cannot fail for this. (3) Minor: the measurement the design rests on does not reproduce. The message of commit b684ca606 and the cli/ast/runtime log entry of 2026-11-11T21:11 say a parser exhausted by one file never builds a tree again and keeps its 2 GiB. On this branch's runtime, after 'a<b,' 16384 times aborts alone, reset() on the same parser builds the reference tree identical to a fresh runtime's, and so does a new parser after deleting the old one. Only the same parser without reset() aborts again. Replacing the runtime stays correct, but the component's log records a false fact as the reason for the design. Assumptions judged: round 1's design replaced rather than patched, accepted. The report stating the trees held and the file's size with both ways out, accepted for one run on a thread; across concurrent runs it is wrong (finding 2). The signal test skipped on Windows, accepted: the helper notices its parent through the IPC channel closing, which Windows has. Beside this issue: issue 656's shape (two dense JSON arrays of 6.8 MiB walked with descendantsOfType) now reads "The parser ran out of memory while rule 'walks' read the syntax trees it was given", with no Aborted() and no blame on check.mjs; only the heading that 655 covers remains, so 656 may be met by this branch. Memory caps came from a sibling container of the dev image (8 GiB or 12 GiB), since the dev container itself has no limit. (+2 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

Red before, green after, run by me: 243 (release/6.2.0 fails as root, tip 33/33 as node and root), 598 (destructuring error on release/6.2.0, served clean on the tip), 599 (exit 0 on release/6.2.0 with tree-sitter-cli 0.26.0, refused on the tip, also on a warm cache with a source-built grammar), 226/344/345 e2e (tip green; on release/6.2.0 the variable case passes the moved-reference branch with exit 0, the dot-file and split cases fail). Read lines: 226.1 'yg check accepts a reference from outside (a flag and an environment variable, documented for GitHub Actions and general CI) ... a change of the block in a branch without that reference's agreement ends in a check of the whole project with a message': met in code (flag, variable, precedence, whole-project notice naming the source), not met in the docs, Important 1. 226.2 'moving the reference to one's own branch in several commits on a push build with a reference from CI gives FAIL; an ordinary PR and main after a merge pass; Grain's sentence stays true': met. Tried to get past it: moving the block and back (measured, alpha fails), dropping the block (whole project, 'not used' notice), the PR merge commit of the moved branch (whole project, fails), --reference HEAD, @, --all, -h, a missing branch (whole project, fail), an empty variable (unset); HEAD@{0} and the branch's own name pass quietly (Minor 3; the own name is the documented reference-branch row). 267.1 canon-sync reports no difference for Yggdrasil (only Grain differs). 267.2 surface-truth.mjs names Althing and no private repository; the AGENTS.md pointer sits outside the managed block and survived yg init --upgrade rewriting that block in a scratch copy; nothing private in the diff. 267.3 green through repo-check. 344.1/344.2 met: git's two files below the root never unmapped, a real loop's third dot file (.permanent) leaves coverage by the documented line; a built-in default would name another tool's folder in Yggdrasil source, so the docs are the right place. 345.1/345.2 met: the split reads the outside twins; a branch that deletes committed verdicts still counts them as its own (the base verdict keys bring them into scope). FINDINGS. Important 1: docs/progressive-mode.md:67-69 tells the reader to 'take the reference out of the file altogether and have the pipeline name it', but a pipeline reference in a project whose config names none is not used: the run gates the whole project with the 'was not used' notice (run: a branch dropping the block, YG_PROGRESSIVE_REFERENCE=main). It contradicts the same page's 'It does not turn the mode on' and the CLI reference; a reader who follows it loses progressive mode. It should say to keep the block and let the pipeline's reference win. Minor 2: source/cli/src/core/progressive-preflight.ts:131-133, fetchCommand reads every slash as remote/branch: --reference release/nope remedies 'git fetch release nope', a dash-leading value 'git fetch origin --all'; the fallback the worker flagged is untested. Minor 3 (pre-existing pattern, filed outside): source/cli/src/core/progressive-scope-resolve.ts:449 refuses HEAD and @ but not reflog forms; --reference HEAD@{0} measures the branch against itself and passes quietly. Minor 4: source/cli/tests/unit/cli/pack.test.ts:383-395, the rewritten test no longer reaches the EACCES/EPERM message of source/cli/src/io/package-store.ts:493-499 ('one of them is not writable'), and no other test does. Minor 5: source/cli/src/cli/check.ts:193 names the project root for git config safe.directory; for a graph below the repository's top level git needs the top level, so the filled-in command does not clear the warning there. (+1 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

- 2026-11-12 00:04 key 20261111T1935-yyck by rev-641-opus · 641 review changes · by rev-641-opus (fresh) · model claude-opus-5-5@high · batch 20261112T0004-bazc · Important 1 (647, commit 9bc2e235b): the branch commits source/cli/node_modules as a symbolic link to the dev container's own node_modules folder (mode 120000), a machine path in the tree. The ignore line node_modules/ matches only a directory, so the link went in unnoticed (docs/node_modules is the same link, untracked). Merged, a fresh clone gets a dangling link, and a checkout where source/cli/node_modules is a real folder or the container's mounted volume must replace that ignored folder with the link: git treats ignored files as expendable, so the merge either fails on the mount point or empties the installed packages. Fix: remove it from the index in its own commit and ignore node_modules without the trailing slash. Important 2 (682): CHANGELOG.md and the 682 changelog say a key pasted into yg-architecture.yaml is shown by its first four characters in every message yg check prints about that file, in text and --json; three are not masked on the tip and print the key whole: type-unknown-parent (parents: [<key>]), aspect-undefined for a type's aspects ([<key>]) and relation-target-type-unknown (relations.uses: [<key>]), text 3 times and --json 6 times each. Either mask them (src/core/checks: the architecture messages) or narrow both changelogs to the file's refusals. Minor 3 (merge with jarl/302-log-merge-integrity, issue 574): a trial merge gives 15 conflicting hunks in source/cli/src/core/log/log-merge-resolve.ts; 302 already reworked the same next steps (the log file plus the re-run command, verifyUnion taking a location object). Taking 302's side in every hunk loses nothing of 649 (the node-not-found masking merges cleanly), but the new test in tests/unit/core/log-merge-resolve.test.ts ('names the log file in what it asks for') merges without a conflict and then calls verifyUnion with a string, so it fails the typecheck: the merger must rewrite it to pass { gitLogPath, rerun }. Minor 4 (661, cli-base.ts endReviewerWork): a group kept after its leader exits is SIGKILLed at a normal exit without checking that it still has members; if the members ended earlier in a long run and the number was reused as another group of the same user, that group is killed. forgetEmptyGroups() before the kill narrows it. Minor 5 (647/670): templates/rules.ts:97, the agent rules every project gets, still says only Ctrl+C or SIGTERM writes the finished verdicts, while docs and the cli reference now name SIGHUP. Minor 6: commit da4dbc2cb carries three issues (641, 648, 650) in one commit. Tried and holding: every new test red on the release source for the reason it names and green on the tip (250 tests); 25 hand-written yg-architecture.yaml refusals print the same text on release and tip, the YAML syntax error names the file and line, and the reviewer verdict for parser-contract on architecture-parser.ts is approved in the lock; SIGHUP to yg and a closed pty during a claude-code and a Copilot review with stand-in reviewers: reviewer stopped, verdict kept, no folder or lock left; SIGKILL: folder and lock left and removed by the next run, a live run's folder kept; 60 leak probes over node, flow, rule, adaptation and architecture files and command flags: every leak left on the tip is identical on release except Important 2. The three tests judged flaky (portal-extract, cli-check-json 9) pass 5 of 5 on the tip with the deterministic cache filled; they read the repository's own graph, so they race only with tests that rewrite its cache in the same run, not with this branch. The repository check log on the tip says All checks passed. (+3 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

- 2026-11-12 00:09 key 20261002T0949-basf by rev-143d-opus · 143 review changes · by rev-143d-opus (fresh) · model claude-opus-5-5 · batch 20261112T0009-nygn · Important (143, the fix 8ee89cea, cost): a content: rule now reads each file it evaluates through one git cat-file call whenever the file's text is not already in hand, and after a commit it almost never is: an incremental index reads only the changed blobs, so the view falls through to load([path]) one file at a time (plugins/grain/engine/commit-view.mjs:47, reached from plugins/grain/engine/arch.mjs:249 and plugins/grain/engine/yggdrasil-graph.mjs:397). In a repository of 5,001 TypeScript files, 5,000 of them unmapped and a node type with when: content: GENERATED-MISC, a cold index is the same on both trees (2.0 s, 5,001 parsed, every text in hand), but the refresh after a one-file commit goes from 0.7-0.9 s at af685b20 to 13-15 s at 8ee89cea (four runs each, 'indexed in' from grain itself), and a git wrapper counted 2 cat-file calls at af685b20 and 5,001 at 8ee89cea for that refresh. That is about 17 times slower on every commit, on a rebuild over the warm cache after a graph edit, and at each end of grain measure whose blobs are cached. The fix the brief names stands: read the files a content rule evaluates through the existing batch reader (one cat-file --batch per 400, as load already does for manifests), for instance by having the view batch-load every listed entry it has not got on its first miss, or graphOwners prefetch the free files before readNodeGraph. · Met, the correctness of the fix: rev-143c's repro rebuilt (coverage.type_level, type misc with when: content: GENERATED-MISC, partial class Money in src/Core and the unmapped src/Misc/MoneyOps.cs, src/App/Late.cs using Money): with the marker uncommitted, af685b20 gives no edge and ambiguous 2, 8ee89cea gives src/App/Late.cs > src/Core/Money.cs and ambiguous 0; after git checkout of the file, grain status at the same HEAD and export still give that edge and 0. With the marker committed both give no edge and ambiguous 2, and taking the marker out uncommitted leaves 2 at the same HEAD, as the commit says. grain measure from the unmarked to the marked commit gives 0 to 2 unresolved references on both trees. grain check is unchanged by the diff: its graphOwners call (arch.mjs:143) passes no view, so fileHead reads the disk as before; grain check and grain measure each build their graph from disk as they did. The new test fails on af685b20 (the uncommitted marker gives edges [] and ambiguous 2) and passes at 8ee89cea, 2 of 2; the committed-marker case passes on both, so it holds that a marker in the commit still counts. Full suite in a scratch clone at 8ee89cea under the gate's full-gate.sh: runes 127 files match v1.1.0 (c5124ca0525e); tests 2386, pass 2380, fail 0, skipped 6 (platform skips only).

- 2026-11-12 00:11 by jarl · decided file-view-reads-what-git-tracks · by jarl
- 2026-11-12 00:11 by jarl · asked a-38 (ratify) · Yggdrasil 6.2.0 and Grain read dependencies only from files git tracks or does not ignore (the decision behind issue 235). Effect: in C and C++ an ignored compile_commands.json (usually generated into build/) is no longer read, so includes through its -I folders give no dependency; in Go an ignored go.work no longer joins modules; an import through a symbolic link gives none. 6.1.0 read all of these from disk. The jarl chose to keep this and say it plainly in the changelog and docs, with the way back (commit the file). Ratify, or say: read those configuration files from disk even when ignored (Grain's index, which reads commits, would then disagree with Yggdrasil on those repositories).

Fetch advice by hand, every case as the worker says: origin + origin/main gives 'git fetch origin main'; origin + release/nope gives 'git fetch origin release/nope'; one remote 'upstream' gives 'git fetch upstream nope' and 'git fetch upstream main'; two remotes a, b without origin give no command for 'nope' and 'git fetch a main' for 'a/main'; no remote gives no command; origin/-x gives no command; -x is refused before any git call. safe.directory: the new unit test covers the path git names and a graph below the top level. The pack refusal test stubs EACCES and reaches the 'not writable' message. 675 and 681: red on d6c28086b and green on the tip, rows recorded. Tried to get past 681: '--end-of-options' as the value is refused; '^main', 'main..HEAD', 'main...HEAD', ':/', 'main^{tree}', 'HEAD:src', 'head', and values with a space or a newline (including 'main<newline>--upload-pack=touch <file>' from the variable) all reach git as one name after --end-of-options, fail to resolve, and fall to the whole project (nothing ran, the file was not created). ':/edit' and the branch's own name pass quietly, which is the same thing as naming one's own branch, the case the pipeline reference closes. A committed dash-led block does not brick the check: the run completes on defaults, fails, and reports config-invalid naming the file and the key to set, with --full, --json and --reference too. --end-of-options needs git 2.24; yg already needs 2.31 (rev-parse --path-format), so no new floor. Record, outside this scope: 675 and 681 still hold no row by the lease holder, which the brief ranks Important; the jarl decides. | Minor: source/cli/src/core/progressive-preflight.ts:138-151, fetchCommand checks only the first character, so a reference that is not a branch name is printed as is in the fix a person copies: 'main --all' gives 'git fetch origin main --all', 'main --upload-pack=<command>' would carry that option into the pasted command, '^main' gives a negative refspec, 'main..HEAD' and 'HEAD:src' print commands that cannot work, and a value with a newline splits the command over two lines. yg itself never runs it. Fix: print a command only when the branch part follows git's ref-name rules (no whitespace or control characters, none of ~^:?*[\, no '..', no leading dash), else the general sentence. Tried to get past 681: '--end-of-options' as the value is refused; '^main', 'main..HEAD', 'main...HEAD', ':/', 'main^{tree}', 'HEAD:src', 'head', and values with a space or a newline (including 'main<newline>--upload-pack=touch <file>' from the variable) all reach git as one name after --end-of-options, fail to resolve, and fall to the whole project (nothing ran, the file was not created). ':/edit' and the branch's own name pass quietly, which is the same thing as naming one's own branch, the case the pipeline reference closes. A committed dash-led block does not brick the check: the run completes on defaults, fails, and reports config-invalid naming the file and the key to set, with --full, --json and --reference too. --end-of-options needs git 2.24; yg already needs 2.31 (rev-parse --path-format), so no new floor. Not re-run here: 598, 599 (round 1 and the jarl's repo-check cover them); pack.test.ts passed again with the touched files. Not run: lowercase 'head' on a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS), where git may resolve it to HEAD; here it does not resolve. Record, outside this scope: 675 and 681 still hold no row by the lease holder, which the brief ranks Important; the jarl decides. | Minor: source/cli/src/core/progressive-preflight.ts:138-151, fetchCommand checks only the first character, so a reference that is not a branch name is printed as is in the fix a person copies: 'main --all' gives 'git fetch origin main --all', 'main --upload-pack=<command>' would carry that option into the pasted command, '^main' gives a negative refspec, 'main..HEAD' and 'HEAD:src' print commands that cannot work, and a value with a newline splits the command over two lines. yg itself never runs it. Fix: print a command only when the branch part follows git's ref-name rules (no whitespace or control characters, none of ~^:?*[\, no '..', no leading dash), else the general sentence. Minor: docs/progressive-mode.md:522-523 says an empty --reference is refused but not that a reference starting with a dash is refused from the flag, the variable and the file. Minor: source/cli/src/core/progressive-scope-resolve.ts:275, when the committed block is refused as config-invalid, a run with --reference says 'this project's committed config names none', but the file names an invalid one (the config-invalid error is printed in the same run).

- 2026-11-12 00:18 key 20261111T1150-vqto by rev-561c-opus · 561 review approve · by rev-561c-opus (fresh) · model claude-opus-5-5 · batch 20261112T0018-nwne · Round 3, approve: round 2's two Importants are met and nothing breaks. Reruns, in sibling containers of the dev image capped at 8 GiB (12 GiB for the timing): the e2e file passes 11 of 11 on the tip; its round-3 tests fail 5 of 5 on ea4c572eb, each for its reason; the touched unit and integration files pass (18 files, 294 tests); the 672 and 673 unit tests fail on ea4c572eb for their reasons. Round 2's repros: with 64 KiB of 'a<b,' and with a 56 MiB dense bundle as a subject of a per-file reviewer rule, yg check, yg check --json, yg check --approve and yg aspect-test --node end in error[internal] on ea4c572eb and in their own reports on the tip; yg drill on a plain reviewer rule ends in error[internal] on ea4c572eb and records the case as unrun with the reason on the tip, passing the other case. --approve calls the reviewer for the 4 other subjects; aspect-test judges them and says 'incomplete'. Side by side (two companion rules whose trees fit alone and not together): no rule is reported for the other rule's files at parallel 4 or 10 (ea4c572eb names src/delta/p4.ts for reads-target at parallel 4 and makes no progress on a rerun); at parallel 4 the tip verifies 6 of 9, then 9 of 9 on a second run; at parallel 10, 4 of 9, then 7 of 9. Plain yg check: the pair is shown as '1 pair with no verdict yet', fix 'yg check --approve (1 reviewer pair · 1 call · paid)', without the cause; the same output's relation-parse-failed names the file and the reason when the relation check reads that language, and --approve names it, so the user has a next step; accepted as the suppress-marker precedent. 672's cost, yg check --approve --only-deterministic on Yggdrasil's own tree, 6776 script pairs, warm relation cache: release 13 workers, fill 15-17 s, command about 21 s, also when the machine reports 8 GiB; tip 13 workers at 29.4 GiB, 7 at 16 GiB (fill 19 s), 3 at 8 GiB (fill 24 s, command 29-30 s, peak about 570 MiB against 1.5 GiB); same report on every run (8285 pairs on the tip). Slower on a many-core machine with little memory, unchanged on a machine of 4 cores; not a reason for changes. The release merge aaa813ce4 equals a recomputed merge of e59abc0c9 and f36bffcc0 in every file but the two conflicted logs (aspect-test log.md, yg-lock.logs.json), resolved by keeping both entries, so 620's and the keys package's changes stand; e2abb6770 touches only logs. scripts/repo-check.sh not run here: the jarl's log of the tip says All checks passed (10703 tests, coverage 97.56/96.55/96.99/91.43, Graph: check PASS with 8285 pairs). Findings, all Minor. (1) Minor, filed outside: --approve's closing summary counts a reviewer pair whose subject the parser has no memory for among provider and configuration failures and advises fixing the reviewer connection (core/review-package.ts:220-222, kind infra). (2) Minor, a known limit: a side-by-side report where the run held trees of its own and the other runs held theirs advises reading fewer trees or leaving the named file out, never lowering parallel (ast/parse-guard.ts:143-150), so at parallel 10 the last pair of each rule run together and fail again on every rerun; reading fewer trees is a real way out. (3) Minor: the per-worker floor MIN_WORKER_FOOTPRINT_BYTES can no longer bind (cli/det-concurrency.ts:121-126: the new term allows at most total/2 GiB workers, the floored estimate total/256 MiB), so the test 'applies a floor to the per-worker estimate' (tests/unit/cli/det-concurrency.test.ts:42) passes with the floor removed; what it protected holds through the new bound. (4) Minor, wording: yg drill's next step for such a case file says to leave it out of the component's mapping and run yg check --approve (core/drill-runner.ts:578), which does not fit a case file; the grouped heading for side-by-side reports still reads 'Companion resolution for ... failed to run on N units (aspect-companion-runtime-error)', without companion.mjs. Assumptions judged: plain check leaving the pair unverified without the cause, accepted (above); failure records and held-tree counts per run, accepted and shown on two real runs; the pool bound against the whole machine with every parser full, accepted. Not run: a Windows host; drill on a rule with a companion (drill does not support one). (+1 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

(4) Minor, wording: yg drill's next step for such a case file says to leave it out of the component's mapping and run yg check --approve (core/drill-runner.ts:578), which does not fit a case file; the grouped heading for side-by-side reports still reads 'Companion resolution for ... failed to run on N units (aspect-companion-runtime-error)', without companion.mjs. Assumptions judged: plain check leaving the pair unverified without the cause, accepted (above); failure records and held-tree counts per run, accepted and shown on two real runs; the pool bound against the whole machine with every parser full, accepted. Not run: a Windows host; drill on a rule with a companion (drill does not support one). (+1 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

Sweep sample: the next steps of type-unknown-parent, architecture-cycle, enforce-strict-without-when, type-without-when-with-mapping, port-aspect, relation-target-forbidden, architecture parents, port consumes, dangling refs (node, port, type, flow), implied-aspect-missing, implies cycle and the predicate checks name files and keys that exist in that situation (flow paths are one level under flows, an adaptation cannot carry when or implies, so the predicate file is right); the re-pinned tests keep what they asserted, the full steps are pinned in checks-concrete-steps.test.ts. Repro, legal C# in three projects: Lib declares namespace N; public class TBase { public class Inner { } } and public class T : TBase { }; Mid references Lib and declares public class Outer : T { }; App references Mid and Lib, declares its own public class T : Outer.Inner { } (a type of its own compilation, warning CS0436) and public class Use { Outer.Inner f; }, plus one file that reaches T's bases outside a reading. Each of three triggers works: an attribute [T] public class A { }; a call T t; void M() { t.Run(); } with an extension Run(this TBase t) in Lib; or a member lookup public class A : T { void M() { Inner.Go(); } }. With App's files declared before Lib's, c5124ca gives App/T.cs:2 -> Lib/TBase.cs and App/Use.cs:3 -> Lib/TBase.cs, and eb99977 gives neither. In the reversed order both agree. Declaring the files in two halves around a resolution shows the same two losses and nothing else. I tried one remedy in a scratch copy, not in the branch: count the lookup's bind and declared callbacks as nesting (csharpKeysDepth++ and -- around both at resolver.mts:433-437). With it all three cases and the split runs match c5124ca, so do 180 random repositories, the bound test still passes, and yg check on eShop takes 4.0 s cold and 1.7 to 2.6 s warm with identical edges. The three cases want catalogue entries. What held, identical to c5124ca: 420 runs of random multi-project repositories over three file orders (partial classes, nested types with bases, dotted and generic bases, aliases, global usings, using static, attributes, method calls, extension methods), and targeted cases: a partial class whose base sits in one part; global usings and aliases reaching a nested type through a base; two file types of one name with different bases; one nested name read inside two outer types; Result and Result<T>; a name that is a namespace in one place and a type in another. Each case was also declared in two halves around a resolution. Both acceptance lines re-run and hold (see the proof rows): the test is red on e955a21 and catches both mutants; the corpus gate shows 0 added and 0 removed; yg check is inside 1.25 of the Runes 1.0.0 baseline on eShop and jellyfin, cold and warm, with the same edges before and after. - 2026-11-12 03:18 key 20261111T1952-eoyp by rev-645-opus · 645 review changes · by rev-645-opus (fresh) · model claude-opus-5-5 · batch 20261112T0318-jgqt · Changes: two Important findings (653, 677); the other eight issues meet their lines. Important (653), src/relations/extractors/rust.mts:338 with test/relations/extractors/rust.test.mjs:253 and :355: the fix drops a use whose first name a block of its own declares as a mod, struct, enum, union, trait or type alias, whatever the edition, but in edition 2015 a use path is relative to the crate root, so the block item does not hide the root's extern crate alias. Repro: the case's own files with edition = "2015" in both manifests, and a line Engine::only_in_crate(); after the use, a function only engine_core's Engine has: cargo check under rustc 1.99.1 compiles it (the block's Engine is reported never constructed), the 2021 variant fails E0599, so rustc binds the extern crate in 2015 and the block module in 2021. c5124ca gives src/lib.rs:6 -> engine in 2015 (right) and in 2021 (wrong); 90c330f gives no edge in either, so the 2021 fix costs a true edge in every 2015 crate of this form. The two unit tests whose expectations lost 'cl::Shadowed', 'cl::V' and 'blocked::G' removed exactly the as-written path the extractor emits for a 2015 crate (rust.mts:341's comment). Wants a catalogue case for the 2015 form; the fix must keep the as-written reading for 2015 and silence it only from 2018. Important (677), the [read] line "Measured on the Rust repositories of the corpus how many manifests omit edition and how many edges change, and either the CHANGELOG's Before you upgrade names it or the behaviour is changed with a test": the measurement holds (I count 293 [package] manifests in the shared corpus cache, ripgrep 12, zed 267, react 13, next-intl 1, none without edition, so no edge changes), but neither branch of the either is done: CHANGELOG.md on 90c330f says nothing about edition 2015 or extern crate in Before you upgrade or elsewhere, 677 carries no changelog entry, and the behaviour did not change. The Why says adopters must learn it before the upgrade; 0 in the corpus does not tell them. Minor (645), docs/api.md:95 and src/relations/resolver.mts:418 still say a reading that names two owners stays ambiguous because the receiver's type is not read and that a consumer's count of ambiguous answers does not move; docs/api.md:97 and byReceiver, in the same release, now read it and turn such readings into a binding. Minor (651), src/relations/extractors/rust.mts:667-668: a crate root not named lib.rs or main.rs (src/bin/tool.rs, examples/, tests/, benches/, build.rs, a [lib] or [[bin]] path) and a file itself loaded through #[path] are mod-rs files to rustc, yet the inline path is prefixed with the file stem: src/bin/tool.rs with mod outer { #[path = "x.rs"] mod x; } records src/bin/tool/outer/x.rs where rustc loads src/bin/outer/x.rs, so x.rs's mod child; still binds the decoy src/bin/outer/x/child.rs on both trees (no regression; the new reading does not reach these roots). Minor (651), test/relations/rust-cases-build.test.mjs:78: CARGO_TARGET_DIR is one fixed folder under the system temporary directory, shared by concurrent runs and never removed (51 MB left after one run), and cargo writes the user's own cargo home; the workflows install no Rust toolchain, so CI always skips both tests and the list-only-shrinks guard holds only where 1.99.1 is installed. Minor (666), src/relations/resolver.mts:376: a private extension method counts for every call of its own file, but C# sees it only inside its class: src/Ext/B.cs declaring static class B { static void Tag(this Order o) } and a class User calling o.Tag() in the same file binds Lib's public Tag; both trees give no B.cs:7 -> Lib (the worker's documented own-file reading; the line says no definer outside its own class). The [read] line of 693, "docs/api.md describes the file view, the C# reachability and onDiagnostic as what they are, with no claim about when or whether the family's tools adopt them": met; lines 69, 71 and 73 describe each and say what a consumer may do, and no sentence names a pickup or a release. What held: all 22 new cases run on c5124ca code: 19 fail there (13 of 16 C#, 3 of 3 Rust including the changed relative-path-forms case, 3 of 4 TypeScript), the 3 passing on both are guard cases; the 31 completed Rust fixtures keep their expectations and give the same answers on c5124ca code; the full suite on 90c330f with rustc 1.99.1: 2649 tests, 2648 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (go), dist identical; corpus gate --tier all for every C#, TypeScript, Rust and Kotlin repository: passed, 0 added and 0 removed everywhere, oracle disagreements all explained (C# oracle skipped, no dotnet here); react -40: all 40 read, each an extensionless react/src/* or react-dom/src/* import under exports ./src/* -> ./src/*, which Node and TypeScript (loadModuleFromFileNoImplicitExtensions) do not resolve; jellyfin +63: all 63 read, each the head type of an is chain under ||, &&, ==, or inside not, bound as the file's usings name it, and the 3 Program.cs explanations match the source (HostWebClient and UseUnixSocket declared once, using static at line 36); the rustc build guard attacked three ways in a scratch copy (a type error in an unlisted case, a listed case delisted, a building case listed): each turns it red; the oracle call-form test fails on the old checker and passes on the new; Kotlin: the position test fails at c6d3826 and passes, 660 damaged variants of 220 moshi and okhttp files give identical facts before and after, the remaining depth-1 difference comes from the grammar's own whole-file parse (annotated_expression with no error), not recovery, and the dropped extractor test is named in 404fa12; the text callback field the Kotlin tree edit sets exists in web-tree-sitter 0.27.0, pinned exactly; API: hasNamespace's accept and takes.receiver are optional additions, both documented in docs/api.md, CsharpTypeLookup is not exported; probes that held: an interface receiver with Tag(this Order) and Tag(this IOrder) binds the IOrder one, a multi-line import type and an export type with the mode clause on the next line read once with the mode; the public Worker drop follows the receiver rule that the first name binding a type gives the edge. The merge with 686, already in release/1.1.0 at da2c874: every finding above survives it unchanged (none sits in code 686 rewrites, except the stale takesCall comment, which moves with it). For the merger: 686 keeps shadowed's answer per name (kept.declared) and this branch makes that answer depend on the calling file's reach, so the merged shadowed must key its cache by name and calling file, or skip it when reach is given, or the hidden-namespace case turns on file order; hintKeys must keep passing fromFile to set members, which 686's version does not; assemblyOnlyIn's fallback should read filesOf; hasNamespace with accept walks a namespace's files on every call outside 686's caches, and byReceiver binds a type per ambiguous call, so 686's 1.25x [compare] wants re-measuring after the merge (this branch on c5124ca: jellyfin 62.9 s, eShop 13.9 s on the gate clock). (+3 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

- 2026-11-12 03:18 key 20261111T2002-jwvd tip by rev-645-opus · 651 tip 90c330fc24443207702575642e206fc588b1e568
- 2026-11-12 03:18 key 20261111T2017-nwsn by rev-645-opus · 653 review changes · by rev-645-opus (fresh) · model claude-opus-5-5 · batch 20261112T0318-jgqt · Changes: two Important findings (653, 677); the other eight issues meet their lines. Important (653), src/relations/extractors/rust.mts:338 with test/relations/extractors/rust.test.mjs:253 and :355: the fix drops a use whose first name a block of its own declares as a mod, struct, enum, union, trait or type alias, whatever the edition, but in edition 2015 a use path is relative to the crate root, so the block item does not hide the root's extern crate alias. Repro: the case's own files with edition = "2015" in both manifests, and a line Engine::only_in_crate(); after the use, a function only engine_core's Engine has: cargo check under rustc 1.99.1 compiles it (the block's Engine is reported never constructed), the 2021 variant fails E0599, so rustc binds the extern crate in 2015 and the block module in 2021. c5124ca gives src/lib.rs:6 -> engine in 2015 (right) and in 2021 (wrong); 90c330f gives no edge in either, so the 2021 fix costs a true edge in every 2015 crate of this form. The two unit tests whose expectations lost 'cl::Shadowed', 'cl::V' and 'blocked::G' removed exactly the as-written path the extractor emits for a 2015 crate (rust.mts:341's comment). Wants a catalogue case for the 2015 form; the fix must keep the as-written reading for 2015 and silence it only from 2018. Important (677), the [read] line "Measured on the Rust repositories of the corpus how many manifests omit edition and how many edges change, and either the CHANGELOG's Before you upgrade names it or the behaviour is changed with a test": the measurement holds (I count 293 [package] manifests in the shared corpus cache, ripgrep 12, zed 267, react 13, next-intl 1, none without edition, so no edge changes), but neither branch of the either is done: CHANGELOG.md on 90c330f says nothing about edition 2015 or extern crate in Before you upgrade or elsewhere, 677 carries no changelog entry, and the behaviour did not change. The Why says adopters must learn it before the upgrade; 0 in the corpus does not tell them. Minor (645), docs/api.md:95 and src/relations/resolver.mts:418 still say a reading that names two owners stays ambiguous because the receiver's type is not read and that a consumer's count of ambiguous answers does not move; docs/api.md:97 and byReceiver, in the same release, now read it and turn such readings into a binding. Minor (651), src/relations/extractors/rust.mts:667-668: a crate root not named lib.rs or main.rs (src/bin/tool.rs, examples/, tests/, benches/, build.rs, a [lib] or [[bin]] path) and a file itself loaded through #[path] are mod-rs files to rustc, yet the inline path is prefixed with the file stem: src/bin/tool.rs with mod outer { #[path = "x.rs"] mod x; } records src/bin/tool/outer/x.rs where rustc loads src/bin/outer/x.rs, so x.rs's mod child; still binds the decoy src/bin/outer/x/child.rs on both trees (no regression; the new reading does not reach these roots). Minor (651), test/relations/rust-cases-build.test.mjs:78: CARGO_TARGET_DIR is one fixed folder under the system temporary directory, shared by concurrent runs and never removed (51 MB left after one run), and cargo writes the user's own cargo home; the workflows install no Rust toolchain, so CI always skips both tests and the list-only-shrinks guard holds only where 1.99.1 is installed. Minor (666), src/relations/resolver.mts:376: a private extension method counts for every call of its own file, but C# sees it only inside its class: src/Ext/B.cs declaring static class B { static void Tag(this Order o) } and a class User calling o.Tag() in the same file binds Lib's public Tag; both trees give no B.cs:7 -> Lib (the worker's documented own-file reading; the line says no definer outside its own class). The [read] line of 693, "docs/api.md describes the file view, the C# reachability and onDiagnostic as what they are, with no claim about when or whether the family's tools adopt them": met; lines 69, 71 and 73 describe each and say what a consumer may do, and no sentence names a pickup or a release. What held: all 22 new cases run on c5124ca code: 19 fail there (13 of 16 C#, 3 of 3 Rust including the changed relative-path-forms case, 3 of 4 TypeScript), the 3 passing on both are guard cases; the 31 completed Rust fixtures keep their expectations and give the same answers on c5124ca code; the full suite on 90c330f with rustc 1.99.1: 2649 tests, 2648 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (go), dist identical; corpus gate --tier all for every C#, TypeScript, Rust and Kotlin repository: passed, 0 added and 0 removed everywhere, oracle disagreements all explained (C# oracle skipped, no dotnet here); react -40: all 40 read, each an extensionless react/src/* or react-dom/src/* import under exports ./src/* -> ./src/*, which Node and TypeScript (loadModuleFromFileNoImplicitExtensions) do not resolve; jellyfin +63: all 63 read, each the head type of an is chain under ||, &&, ==, or inside not, bound as the file's usings name it, and the 3 Program.cs explanations match the source (HostWebClient and UseUnixSocket declared once, using static at line 36); the rustc build guard attacked three ways in a scratch copy (a type error in an unlisted case, a listed case delisted, a building case listed): each turns it red; the oracle call-form test fails on the old checker and passes on the new; Kotlin: the position test fails at c6d3826 and passes, 660 damaged variants of 220 moshi and okhttp files give identical facts before and after, the remaining depth-1 difference comes from the grammar's own whole-file parse (annotated_expression with no error), not recovery, and the dropped extractor test is named in 404fa12; the text callback field the Kotlin tree edit sets exists in web-tree-sitter 0.27.0, pinned exactly; API: hasNamespace's accept and takes.receiver are optional additions, both documented in docs/api.md, CsharpTypeLookup is not exported; probes that held: an interface receiver with Tag(this Order) and Tag(this IOrder) binds the IOrder one, a multi-line import type and an export type with the mode clause on the next line read once with the mode; the public Worker drop follows the receiver rule that the first name binding a type gives the edge. The merge with 686, already in release/1.1.0 at da2c874: every finding above survives it unchanged (none sits in code 686 rewrites, except the stale takesCall comment, which moves with it). For the merger: 686 keeps shadowed's answer per name (kept.declared) and this branch makes that answer depend on the calling file's reach, so the merged shadowed must key its cache by name and calling file, or skip it when reach is given, or the hidden-namespace case turns on file order; hintKeys must keep passing fromFile to set members, which 686's version does not; assemblyOnlyIn's fallback should read filesOf; hasNamespace with accept walks a namespace's files on every call outside 686's caches, and byReceiver binds a type per ambiguous call, so 686's 1.25x [compare] wants re-measuring after the merge (this branch on c5124ca: jellyfin 62.9 s, eShop 13.9 s on the gate clock). - 2026-11-12 03:18 key 20261111T2152-kfpy by rev-645-opus · 667 review changes · by rev-645-opus (fresh) · model claude-opus-5-5 · batch 20261112T0318-jgqt · Changes: two Important findings (653, 677); the other eight issues meet their lines. Important (653), src/relations/extractors/rust.mts:338 with test/relations/extractors/rust.test.mjs:253 and :355: the fix drops a use whose first name a block of its own declares as a mod, struct, enum, union, trait or type alias, whatever the edition, but in edition 2015 a use path is relative to the crate root, so the block item does not hide the root's extern crate alias. Repro: the case's own files with edition = "2015" in both manifests, and a line Engine::only_in_crate(); after the use, a function only engine_core's Engine has: cargo check under rustc 1.99.1 compiles it (the block's Engine is reported never constructed), the 2021 variant fails E0599, so rustc binds the extern crate in 2015 and the block module in 2021. c5124ca gives src/lib.rs:6 -> engine in 2015 (right) and in 2021 (wrong); 90c330f gives no edge in either, so the 2021 fix costs a true edge in every 2015 crate of this form. The two unit tests whose expectations lost 'cl::Shadowed', 'cl::V' and 'blocked::G' removed exactly the as-written path the extractor emits for a 2015 crate (rust.mts:341's comment). Wants a catalogue case for the 2015 form; the fix must keep the as-written reading for 2015 and silence it only from 2018. Important (677), the [read] line "Measured on the Rust repositories of the corpus how many manifests omit edition and how many edges change, and either the CHANGELOG's Before you upgrade names it or the behaviour is changed with a test": the measurement holds (I count 293 [package] manifests in the shared corpus cache, ripgrep 12, zed 267, react 13, next-intl 1, none without edition, so no edge changes), but neither branch of the either is done: CHANGELOG.md on 90c330f says nothing about edition 2015 or extern crate in Before you upgrade or elsewhere, 677 carries no changelog entry, and the behaviour did not change. The Why says adopters must learn it before the upgrade; 0 in the corpus does not tell them. Minor (645), docs/api.md:95 and src/relations/resolver.mts:418 still say a reading that names two owners stays ambiguous because the receiver's type is not read and that a consumer's count of ambiguous answers does not move; docs/api.md:97 and byReceiver, in the same release, now read it and turn such readings into a binding. Minor (651), src/relations/extractors/rust.mts:667-668: a crate root not named lib.rs or main.rs (src/bin/tool.rs, examples/, tests/, benches/, build.rs, a [lib] or [[bin]] path) and a file itself loaded through #[path] are mod-rs files to rustc, yet the inline path is prefixed with the file stem: src/bin/tool.rs with mod outer { #[path = "x.rs"] mod x; } records src/bin/tool/outer/x.rs where rustc loads src/bin/outer/x.rs, so x.rs's mod child; still binds the decoy src/bin/outer/x/child.rs on both trees (no regression; the new reading does not reach these roots). Minor (651), test/relations/rust-cases-build.test.mjs:78: CARGO_TARGET_DIR is one fixed folder under the system temporary directory, shared by concurrent runs and never removed (51 MB left after one run), and cargo writes the user's own cargo home; the workflows install no Rust toolchain, so CI always skips both tests and the list-only-shrinks guard holds only where 1.99.1 is installed. Minor (666), src/relations/resolver.mts:376: a private extension method counts for every call of its own file, but C# sees it only inside its class: src/Ext/B.cs declaring static class B { static void Tag(this Order o) } and a class User calling o.Tag() in the same file binds Lib's public Tag; both trees give no B.cs:7 -> Lib (the worker's documented own-file reading; the line says no definer outside its own class). The [read] line of 693, "docs/api.md describes the file view, the C# reachability and onDiagnostic as what they are, with no claim about when or whether the family's tools adopt them": met; lines 69, 71 and 73 describe each and say what a consumer may do, and no sentence names a pickup or a release. What held: all 22 new cases run on c5124ca code: 19 fail there (13 of 16 C#, 3 of 3 Rust including the changed relative-path-forms case, 3 of 4 TypeScript), the 3 passing on both are guard cases; the 31 completed Rust fixtures keep their expectations and give the same answers on c5124ca code; the full suite on 90c330f with rustc 1.99.1: 2649 tests, 2648 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (go), dist identical; corpus gate --tier all for every C#, TypeScript, Rust and Kotlin repository: passed, 0 added and 0 removed everywhere, oracle disagreements all explained (C# oracle skipped, no dotnet here); react -40: all 40 read, each an extensionless react/src/* or react-dom/src/* import under exports ./src/* -> ./src/*, which Node and TypeScript (loadModuleFromFileNoImplicitExtensions) do not resolve; jellyfin +63: all 63 read, each the head type of an is chain under ||, &&, ==, or inside not, bound as the file's usings name it, and the 3 Program.cs explanations match the source (HostWebClient and UseUnixSocket declared once, using static at line 36); the rustc build guard attacked three ways in a scratch copy (a type error in an unlisted case, a listed case delisted, a building case listed): each turns it red; the oracle call-form test fails on the old checker and passes on the new; Kotlin: the position test fails at c6d3826 and passes, 660 damaged variants of 220 moshi and okhttp files give identical facts before and after, the remaining depth-1 difference comes from the grammar's own whole-file parse (annotated_expression with no error), not recovery, and the dropped extractor test is named in 404fa12; the text callback field the Kotlin tree edit sets exists in web-tree-sitter 0.27.0, pinned exactly; API: hasNamespace's accept and takes.receiver are optional additions, both documented in docs/api.md, CsharpTypeLookup is not exported; probes that held: an interface receiver with Tag(this Order) and Tag(this IOrder) binds the IOrder one, a multi-line import type and an export type with the mode clause on the next line read once with the mode; the public Worker drop follows the receiver rule that the first name binding a type gives the edge. - 2026-11-12 03:19 key 20261112T0314-mmbu by jarl · 703 body · acceptance · was "- [test] A graph made by yg init asks for no log entry on any node type and no ratification of any rule (the default config and every template), and yg check on a fresh project with a code change stays green without a log entry or a ratification; turning either on is one documented setting \u00b7 by: cd source/cli && npm test\n- [test] yg prime, the rules and digest blocks yg init writes, and every knowledge page say nowhere that yg check --approve must not be run, and describe it as the normal way to record verdicts, with the cost of reviewer calls stated \u00b7 by: cd source/cli && npm test\n- [read] yg prime and its derivatives (rules.ts, digest.ts, knowledge pages, default config comments, docs, examples, the init flow's own suggestions) steer an agent first to describe the project in yg-architecture.yaml with node types and when predicates, to map by the broadest wildcard that fits rather than single file paths, and to write rules (aspects) hierarchically, with yg-node.yaml files for what the types cannot say; an inventory of every place changed is in the evidence\n- [test] The golden corpus, the docs output samples and the rules digest are regenerated and agree with the new guidance, and yg init --upgrade on an existing graph changes no setting the user chose \u00b7 by: cd source/cli && npm test" · by jarl

Reproduced: one fill with two dense 6.8 MiB JSON arrays walked by a rule on one node and a 70 MiB text file read on another prints '1 script rule pair left unverified because the parser ran out of memory ... (src/more/transcript.txt)', a file the parser never read; tests/unit/core/fill-report.test.ts:145 (the mixed case) asserts the same list on both lines, so the test pins the fault. Keep one list per cause. Important (663): no proof row and no test for the line. My own run on d2cc7b6af and fbf372dab does not reproduce it: plain yg check on 2,000,000 numbers (digits 4.0 MB, spaced 6.4 MB, nested 4.0 MB) imported from another node takes 6.2 to 6.7 s first and 0.16 to 0.18 s second on both trees, 9.1 s with a yg-suppress marker in the file, 9.4 s under a rule reading file.ast; the evidence row is recorded, and the line needs the director's call (a test with a stated bound, or the issue closed as not reproducing). Minor (639): the fill's done line still counts these pairs as failed ('0 passed · 0 refused · 2 failed'). Minor, outside: ast/parse-guard.ts:123, :147, :162 and :175 end a script rule's parser-memory report with 'then run yg check --approve', which starts paid reviewer pairs, the fault 611 fixed in the tree-too-large report. Checked and holding: every test red on the base for the stated reason (41 failed there) and green on the tip (262 passed); 560's scan gives the base's markers, lines and reasons for a token split at the 1 MiB read, 2-byte and 4-byte characters split there, CRLF and a Markdown fence across it; 580 passes under 256 MiB with a rule reading one file's text and with a rule reporting every file; 611 ctx.parseAst on a 70 MiB file peaks at 694 MB against 688 MB for file.ast, so no new memory cost; 656's 'no code needed beyond the cause' holds (the base already replaced the worker and printed no Aborted()); 689's floor is dead (bounded by total/256 MiB, always looser than the worst-case bound); the new --json causes are in the UnverifiedCause type, the schema and docs/cli-reference.md. 611 line 2 [read] holds: the tree report reads 'asked for the syntax tree of <file>, N bytes, over the 536870888 characters of text a syntax tree can be built from' and its next ends 'then run yg check --approve --only-deterministic'. Tried against the guards: a symlinked companion (stat follows it), a companion of exactly the limit (read), a marker in a string literal of a file over 64 MiB (waives, as docs/reviewers.md now says). (+1 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)

- 2026-11-12 03:43 key 20261011T2328-vxal by rev-574g-opus · 302 review changes · by rev-574g-opus (fresh) · model claude-opus-5-5 · batch 20261112T0343-jkit · Important 1, docs/the-lock.md:153 and the CHANGELOG 574 entry (CHANGELOG.md:123): the reason given for the first limit is not true, and the outcome is left out. The text says the commit then records the entry only in its rewritten form. Reproduced on f27ab8a0c, by a fixup squashed with git rebase -i --autosquash and by an amend at an edit pause: the folded commit's committed baseline is still the one recorded from the first form, so yg check on that branch reports log-integrity prefix_modified. At a rebase stop and at a cherry-pick stop, yg log merge-resolve --node app exits 0 and records a baseline over the rewrite. After the continue, yg check reports only the merge's log-entry-missing, so the rewrite reads green once the merge entry is written. Without a stop the branch stays red. Issue 702's Why says this correctly. Fix: say that the commit's log no longer matches its own baseline, so the stop holds nothing from it, and that the rewrite then passes yg check, while the same branch without a stop stays red. Important 2, source/cli/src/core/log/log-merge-resolve.ts:850 (log-merge-sides-unreadable) and :1056 (the unreadable replay stop): the printed step git rev-parse --verify <ref> <ref> [<base>] always fails with fatal: Needed a single revision, because --verify takes exactly one ref. So it never shows which ref does not resolve: git rev-parse --verify nosuch main and git rev-parse --verify HEAD HEAD~1 both exit 128 with that same line. The merge kept this branch's wording over the release's git rev-parse <refs> from bcb8d7834. That one works: it prints the ref that does not resolve. The unit test (tests/unit/core/log-merge-resolve.test.ts:423,428) pins the text but never runs the command. Fix: drop --verify, or give one git rev-parse --verify per ref. Checked and holding: the revert limit reproduces as written. A branch that records an entry and reverts it is refused at the next rebase stop with log-merge-history-rewritten. The printed step (abort, rebase -i, edit the revert commit, restore the log from HEAD~1, amend, continue, rebase again) works as printed, and the stop then reconciles. yg check and the two-sided merge form accept the same branch. The other 13 of the 15 resolved hunks keep or improve on the release's next steps: each names the log file and the command to run again (verifyUnion and verifyReplayResolution through { gitLogPath, rerun }, clash, dropped-entry, log-missing). maskSecretShapes stands in node-not-found, and cli-validation-codes passes 75 of 75. Every file only one side touched is byte-identical to that side, so the parser-memory and Runes changes came in whole. The clean 3-way merges of the shared files match the merge commit, apart from the 7-line rewrite of the release's verifyUnion test. f27ab8a0c touches only the lock and event files. The log, merge and lock tests, unit and e2e (39 files, 585 tests, among them cli-merge-driver 48 and cli-merge-replay-target 24), pass on the built tip. The one red, check-lock's git ls-files case, came from my extraction not being a git repository; it passes once the extraction is one. The limits text is in plain words and does not run the product down.

- 2026-11-12 03:52 key 20261112T0317-snch by w-690-sonnet · 704 evidence · Assumed: mask in the listings rather than refuse at load. The key shape (a provider prefix, then 20 or more name characters holding an uppercase letter or a digit) also matches ordinary names (a provider prefix such as sk- followed by a long report title), so refusing at load would turn a working repository red, while masking costs such a name only its tail in four listings. Yggdrasil also states elsewhere that it never refuses a configuration over where a key sits. A masked name cannot be typed back as an argument; the owner of such a name has to rename it anyway, since a committed key is already exposed. yg check's own grouped 'at:' listing still prints a key-shaped rule name whole; it is outside the four listings of the issue and is filed under Found.
- 2026-11-12 03:52 key 20261112T0038-byfn by w-690-sonnet · 690 evidence · Assumed: no CHANGELOG entry, because an adopter on the previous version sees nothing: the package exports resolve to the same entries, and the warning removed is only on this repository's own check. The architecture change is exactly two uses relations (rule-script to ast-adapter, test-fixture to ast-adapter); the graph also needed the two nodes graph-rules and cli/tests/fixtures to declare a uses relation to cli/ast/report, which the check named.
- 2026-11-12 03:52 key 20261112T0250-vtrl by w-690-sonnet · 699 evidence · Assumed: the 'dry run that reports and skips a unit' is yg aspect-test --dry-run (a unit whose prompt cannot be assembled is reported and skipped, then the run exited 0); yg check --approve --dry-run is documented to exit 0 always and stays so. The stamp reads 'yg aspect-test: incomplete — N of M units could not be previewed: <unit keys>', the live path's incomplete stamp. The second half of the line (a type-covered file's pair carrying the parser-memory or text-limit cause) cannot be built or proved on release/6.2.0: those causes (parser-out-of-memory, file-over-text-limit) exist only on jarl/560-memory-rest, not yet merged, so it is NOT done and needs this issue re-sent after 560 lands.

- 2026-11-12 04:00 key 20261111T1952-eoyp by rev-645b-opus · 645 review approve · by rev-645b-opus (fresh) · model claude-opus-5-5 · batch 20261112T0400-cijh · Approve: round 1's two Important findings are closed, the merge of 686 loses nothing, one Minor. 653: the block item is emitted as use::1::<block>::<path>, read as written in 2015 and as no file from 2018 on; the case's files with a call only the dependency's Engine has, in edition 2015, 2018, 2021, no edition key, workspace edition 2015 and 2021, a nested module file in 2015 and 2021, and grouped and glob uses: cargo check under rustc 1.99.1 binds the extern crate in every 2015 form and the block module (E0599) in every later one, and 2b21a12 gives the edge at the use in exactly the 2015 forms; the restored unit expectations ('use::1::<block>::cl::Shadowed', '…cl::V', '…blocked::G') are the as-written reading a 2015 crate needs. 677 [read] 'Measured on the Rust repositories of the corpus how many manifests omit edition and how many edges change, and either the CHANGELOG's Before you upgrade names it or the behaviour is changed with a test': met by the Before you upgrade fragment on the issue, the loop's form for the final pass; its claims hold: 1.0.1 never reads the edition, on 2b21a12 a manifest with no edition gives no edge for a use of a dependency without extern crate and edition 2018 gives it, and the fresh zed clone (269 manifests) has no package without an edition. 693 [read] 'docs/api.md describes the file view, the C# reachability and onDiagnostic as what they are, with no claim about when or whether the family's tools adopt them': met; docs/api.md:95 now says two owners stay ambiguous only without a written receiver type and points to the receiver paragraph, and the resolver comment says the same. Merge 7896179 against both parents (remerge diff read): shadowed keeps 686's per-name answer and adds the per-name-and-file answer only with reach, memberKeys goes through csharpMemberKeys with the calling file, assemblyOnlyIn and hintFiles read filesOf and hintKeys as 686 does and keep this branch's private-extension and byReceiver steps; the non-C# shadow path drops the reach test, which loses nothing since only C# emits shadow. The cache is keyed right: 686's random-order test and the new hidden-namespace case pass, and both fail with the key by name only (scratch mutant); on 1000 random multi-project repositories with nested namespaces hidden across project reach (3000 whole runs over three file orders, 3000 split runs declared in two halves around a resolution) 2b21a12 equals a copy that never keeps the per-file answer in every run, with no order or split difference, while the name-only mutant differs in 163 repositories. Speed, same machine, alternating: 686 eShop 2.8 and 2.8 s, jellyfin 27.1 and 26.2 s; 2b21a12 eShop 3.0 and 2.4 s, jellyfin 26.0 and 22.3 s, within the noise. npm run check's steps on a scratch extraction with rustc 1.99.1: 2667 tests, 2666 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (go), both build tests ran, the four new path cases and the 2015 case build, dist identical, no leftover folder in the temporary directory; corpus verify --tier all: 33 repositories passed, 0 added and 0 removed; oracles for zed and ripgrep: cargo 269 and 12 checked, 0 disagreements. zed was not broken: its manifest entry is a sparse clone of Cargo.toml files for the Cargo oracle, so 0 files parsed is by design, and the clone moved aside is identical to the fresh one (same commit, same 269 files). Minor (651), src/relations/resolve-path.mts:122: holdsModulesBeside takes any file named lib.rs or main.rs for a module root by its name, but a module file of that name that is not a crate root is a non-mod-rs file: src/lib.rs mod a; src/a.rs mod lib; src/a/lib.rs mod outer { #[path = "loaded.rs"] mod x; } builds under rustc 1.99.1 with only src/a/lib/outer/loaded.rs, while 2b21a12 reads src/a/outer/loaded.rs and gives a false edge src/a/outer/loaded.rs:1 -> decoy where that file exists; asking crateRootFor for lib.rs and main.rs, as for a root of another name, would close it. Commits name their issue, the fixes are further commits, the rust rev moved 24 to 26 with its test, the catalogue count 961, no test, check or guard weakened.

- 2026-11-12 04:06 key 20261011T2328-vxal by rev-574h-opus · 302 review changes · by rev-574h-opus (fresh) · model claude-opus-5-5 · batch 20261112T0406-wkpv · Important, Yggdrasil docs/the-lock.md:153, CHANGELOG.md:154 and 574's changelog field: the new sentence 'Without a stop, yg check still refuses the branch' is false. Reproduced on d9b4c8ecf in a scratch project made by yg init (its merge drivers installed): a branch whose entry A1 was reworded by an amend in the commit that recorded it is refused on its own (log-integrity prefix_modified), but git merge --no-ff of it into a main that added its own entry, and git rebase main that the drivers settle without stopping, both give yg check PASS, because the merged lock keeps the merge base's baseline when both sides moved it and nothing then holds the first form. The same merge passes on release/6.2.0, so the code gap is older (filed outside); the sentence that denies it is new. The limit should say the rewrite passes any merge, rebase or cherry-pick that combines it with a branch that also moved the log, and that only the branch alone is refused. Minor, same places: 'after --continue yg check asks only for the log entry of the combination' holds only where the node's type has log_required; on a plain type yg check passes straight after --continue. Minor, source/cli/src/core/log/log-merge-resolve.ts:850: the merge-form step 'git rev-parse <refs> to see which ref does not resolve' exits 0 and names nothing when every ref resolves but the log blob is missing (the cause the replay step now meets with git fsck), or when a side has the name of a working-tree path (--theirs src prints 'src', exit 0). Minor, source/cli/tests/unit/core/log-merge-resolve.test.ts:60-66: printedCheck was put between expectedBaselineFromContent's doc comment and that function, so the comment now stands above the wrong function. Confirmed good: at a stop merge-resolve exits 0 and records a baseline over the rewrite, and the rewrite then passes, as written; the printed commands name a missing ref (git rev-parse main nosuch), a missing base (nobase), and at a cherry-pick stop a deleted tree or log blob of the picked commit (git fsck --connectivity-only: missing tree/blob and the commit that links it); the two new tests fail on f27ab8a0c with the tip's test file (2 failed, 85 passed) and pass on the tip (87 passed); git diff f27ab8a0c..d9b4c8ecf touches only the two steps, the two texts, the tests, the log entry and the lock files; yg check --approve --only-deterministic on the extracted tip passes. (+1 more lines, whole text in the issue's Reviews section)
